short_description.id: Kadal Milton adalah kriptid dalam cerita rakyat Kentucky, kadal besar sepanjang sekitar 15 kaki yang dilaporkan terlihat di tempat rongsokan dekat Milton pada musim panas 1975.
short_description.en: The Milton Lizard is a cryptid of Kentucky folklore, a big lizard about 15 feet long reported at a junkyard near Milton in the summer of 1975.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Kentucky, Kadal Milton adalah makhluk yang digambarkan menyerupai biawak sepanjang 15 kaki yang konon terlihat dekat kota Milton, di Trimble County, pada musim panas 1975. Makhluk itu pertama kali terlihat pada Juli oleh Clarence "Tuffy" Cable, salah satu pengelola Blue Grass Body Shop, tempat rongsokan dan pembongkaran mobil di utara Milton; ia melihat kadal itu keluar dari balik bangkai kendaraan dan mendesis kepadanya beberapa kali.
long_description.en: The Milton Lizard belongs to Kentucky folklore: a creature said to resemble a monitor lizard some 15 feet long, reportedly seen near the town of Milton, in Trimble County, in the summer of 1975. Clarence "Tuffy" Cable, who helped manage the Blue Grass Body Shop, a junkyard and car-wrecking business north of Milton, first saw it in July; he watched the lizard come out from behind wrecked vehicles, and it hissed at him several times.

long_description.id: Katalog yang merangkum kasus ini mencatat makhluk tersebut berbadan kadal dengan garis dan bintik hitam putih, bagian bawah mulut berwarna putih, dan mata besar mirip mata katak. Pada 27 Juli saudara Cable, Garrett, melihat tumpukan kap mobil tua bergetar dan bergerak ketika kepala dan bahu kadal itu muncul dari bawah puing. Keesokan harinya Cable melihat kadal itu lagi, kali ini tampak lebih besar, hampir 15 kaki; setelah ia melempar batu, makhluk itu mendesis dan lari ke semak-semak, dan Cable menembak ke arah semak tanpa dapat memastikan apakah ia mengenainya.
long_description.en: The catalog summarizing the case records the entity as having a lizard body with black and white stripes and speckles, white beneath the mouth, and large frog-like eyes. On July 27 Cable's brother Garrett, working in the junkyard, saw a heap of old car hoods start to shake and shift as the lizard's head and shoulders rose from under the wreckage. The next day Cable saw the lizard again, this time apparently larger, nearly 15 feet long; after he threw a rock at it, it hissed and fled into some brush, and Cable fired toward the brush without being certain he hit it.

long_description.id: Pada awal Agustus, regu pencari menyisir sekitar tempat rongsokan itu tetapi tidak menemukan bukti. Cable berteori bahwa telur di salah satu kendaraan rongsok yang pernah mereka beli dari negara bagian barat menetas oleh panas di tempat rongsokan. Seorang penyusun katalog mencatat bahwa kisah di koran lokal terjadi pada musim panas dan melibatkan dua bersaudara pekerja tempat rongsokan, sedangkan kriptozoolog dan peneliti Fortean melaporkan "manusia kadal" raksasa berkaki dua di hutan dekat tempat itu.
long_description.en: In early August a search party combed the area around the junkyard but found no evidence. Cable theorized that eggs in one of the wrecked vehicles bought earlier from a western state had hatched in the junkyard's heat. A catalog compiler notes that the local-newspaper story took place in summer and involved two junkyard-worker brothers, whereas cryptozoologists and Fortean researchers report a giant biped "lizard man" in the woods near the junkyard.

summary.id: Clarence Cable melihat kadal itu pada Juli dan saudaranya Garrett melihatnya pada 27 Juli; keesokan harinya Cable melihat kadal yang tampak lebih besar, melemparinya batu, dan menembak ke semak-semak tanpa dapat memastikan apakah ia mengenai makhluk itu. Regu pencari pada awal Agustus tidak menemukan bukti.
summary.en: Clarence Cable saw the lizard in July and his brother Garrett saw it on July 27; the next day Cable saw a larger-looking one, threw a rock at it and fired into the brush without being certain he hit the creature. A search party in early August found no evidence.

short_description.id: Mujina adalah istilah Jepang lama untuk teledu atau tanuki; dalam cerita rakyat mujina digambarkan sebagai yōkai pengubah wujud yang menipu manusia.
short_description.en: Mujina is an old Japanese term for the badger or tanuki; in folklore the mujina is depicted as a shapeshifting yōkai that deceives humans.

long_description.id: Mujina adalah istilah Jepang lama yang terutama merujuk pada teledu Jepang tetapi secara tradisional pada tanuki, sehingga menimbulkan kebingungan. Dalam wujud aslinya mujina dikatakan berwajah seperti rakun dengan tubuh teledu. Sebuah ensiklopedia Jepang mencatat bahwa dahulu tanuki disebut muji atau mujina, namun hal itu tidak selalu pasti dan ada daerah yang menyebut keduanya mujina.
long_description.en: Mujina is an old Japanese term primarily for the Japanese badger but traditionally for the tanuki, which causes confusion. In its natural form the mujina is said to have a raccoon-like face and a badger's body. A Japanese encyclopedia notes that the tanuki was anciently called muji or mujina, but this is not certain and some regions call both animals mujina.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat, mujina seperti kitsune dan tanuki digambarkan sebagai yōkai yang menipu manusia. Mujina dapat berubah menjadi komet, tiang pagar, batu, pohon, dan sebagainya, dan salah satu wujud kesukaannya adalah pendeta Buddha berjubah hitam. Ia juga dikatakan menggembungkan perutnya dan menabuhnya sambil bernyanyi, serta menciptakan "api hantu" yang menyerupai will-o'-the-wisp. Wujud ubahannya tidak selalu stabil: bila tertidur, penampilannya dapat terurai.
long_description.en: In folklore the mujina, like the tanuki, is depicted as a yōkai that deceives humans. It can turn into comets, fence posts, stones, trees and more, and one of its favorite forms is a black-garbed Buddhist priest. It is also said to inflate its belly and drum on it while singing, and to create a "ghost-fire" resembling will-o'-the-wisps. Its transformation is not always stable: if it falls asleep its appearance can come undone.

long_description.id: Mujina pertama kali tampak dalam sastra di Nihon Shoki, pada bagian tentang tahun ke-35 Permaisuri Suiko (627). Di wilayah Shimōsa mereka disebut kabukiri-kozō, dan di Sado disebut Tonchibō dan juga dianggap seperti wujud dewa gunung. Mujina dikenal sebagai penipu yang gemar bercanda tanpa niat jahat, namun dipercaya berhati lembut dan tahu berterima kasih. Kebingungan istilah ini pernah berdampak hukum: pada 1924 di Prefektur Tochigi seorang pemburu membunuh anjing rakun yang ia kira bernama mujina.
long_description.en: The earliest literary appearance is in the Nihon Shoki, in the section on the 35th year of Empress Suiko (627). In the Shimōsa region they are called kabukiri-kozō, and on Sado they are called Tonchibō and also thought of as resembling a mountain deity. The mujina is known as a trickster fond of harmless pranks, yet is believed to have a gentle heart and to know gratitude. The confusion over the term once had legal consequences: in 1924 in Tochigi Prefecture a hunter killed a raccoon dog he believed to be called a mujina.

statement.id: Di wilayah Shimōsa, mereka disebut kabukiri-kozō dan berubah menjadi kozō (biksu cilik) yang mengenakan kimono aneh yang pendek dan berkepala potongan pendek seperti kappa.
statement.en: In the Shimōsa region they are called kabukiri-kozō and would shapeshift into a kozō (little monk) wearing a strangely short kimono and a kappa-like bobbed head.

claims.quote: 民俗 ムジナはタヌキと同じく人間を化かす，また大入道その他の怪物の姿で人をおどすともいう。

statement.id: Seperti tanuki, mujina menipu manusia, dan dikatakan pula menakuti orang dengan menyamar sebagai 大入道 atau monster lain.
statement.en: Like the tanuki, the mujina deceives humans, and is also said to frighten people in the form of a 大入道 or other monsters.

claims.quote: 佐渡ではトンチボウと呼んで山の神の姿のようにも考え，またこれにまつわる伝承が残っていた。また，長野県北境の山中ではバンブクといって腹に毛のないものが化けるなどともいっていた。

statement.id: Di Sado, mujina disebut Tonchibō dan juga dianggap seperti wujud dewa gunung, dan ada cerita yang berkaitan dengannya; di pegunungan perbatasan utara Prefektur Nagano disebut Banbuku, dikatakan yang perutnya tak berbulu dapat berubah wujud.
statement.en: On Sado it was called Tonchibō and also thought of as resembling a mountain deity, with related traditions preserved; in the mountains on the northern border of Nagano Prefecture it was called Banbuku, and one with a hairless belly was said to transform.

claims.quote: 古くはタヌキを指してムジあるいはムジナと呼び，アナグマをマミあるいはササグマと呼んだという。しかし，これは必ずしも確かではなく，タヌキとアナグマの双方をムジナと呼ぶ地方もある。

statement.id: Konon dahulu tanuki disebut muji atau mujina dan teledu disebut mami atau sasaguma, tetapi hal itu tidak selalu pasti, dan ada daerah yang menyebut tanuki maupun teledu sebagai mujina.
statement.en: It is said that anciently the tanuki was called muji or mujina and the badger mami or sasaguma, but this is not necessarily certain, and in some regions both tanuki and badger are called mujina.

claims.quote: In Tochigi Prefecture in 1924, a hunter killed a raccoon dog, which he believed to be called a mujina.

statement.id: Pada 1924 di Prefektur Tochigi, seorang pemburu membunuh seekor anjing rakun yang ia kira bernama mujina.
statement.en: In 1924 in Tochigi Prefecture, a hunter killed a raccoon dog which he believed to be called a mujina.

claims.quote: Like the other yōkai, the mujina is a notorious trickster, and enjoys using their shapeshifting to play harmless pranks.

statement.id: Seperti yōkai lain, mujina adalah penipu yang terkenal dan gemar memakai kemampuan berubah wujud untuk bercanda tanpa niat jahat.
statement.en: Like other yōkai, the mujina is a notorious trickster and enjoys using its shapeshifting to play harmless pranks.

claims.quote: It is believed that although these creatures can be extremely chaotic, they have a gentle heart, and know how to be grateful.

statement.id: Dipercaya bahwa walau bisa sangat kacau, makhluk ini berhati lembut dan tahu berterima kasih.
statement.en: It is believed that although these creatures can be extremely chaotic, they have a gentle heart and know how to be grateful.

topic.en: Which animal the term mujina refers to

summary.id: Terutama merujuk pada teledu Jepang, tetapi secara tradisional pada anjing rakun (tanuki).
summary.en: Primarily the Japanese badger, but traditionally the raccoon dog (tanuki).

summary.id: Dahulu tanuki disebut muji atau mujina dan teledu disebut mami atau sasaguma, tetapi hal ini tidak pasti dan beberapa daerah menyebut keduanya mujina.
summary.en: The tanuki was anciently called muji or mujina and the badger mami or sasaguma, but this is uncertain and some regions call both mujina.

short_description.id: Nguruvilu adalah makhluk berkepala rubah dan bertubuh ular dari agama Mapuche yang menyambar orang di danau dan sungai [nguruvilu-c01, nguruvilu-c02, nguruvilu-c03].
short_description.en: The Nguruvilu is a fox-headed, snake-bodied creature of Mapuche religion that seizes people in lakes and rivers [nguruvilu-c01, nguruvilu-c02, nguruvilu-c03].

long_description.id: Nguruvilu adalah makhluk legenda dari agama Mapuche [nguruvilu-c01]. Namanya berarti "rubah" + "ular" [nguruvilu-c04], sesuai wujudnya yang berkepala rubah dan bertubuh ular [nguruvilu-c02]. Ia menyambar orang yang mengarungi air dengan ekornya dan memangsa mereka [nguruvilu-c03], sehingga penduduk asli menghindari mandi di danau tempatnya berada [nguruvilu-c05].
long_description.en: The Nguruvilu is a legendary creature of Mapuche religion [nguruvilu-c01]. Its name means "fox" + "serpent" [nguruvilu-c04], matching its fox head and snake body [nguruvilu-c02]. It snatches waders with its tail and devours them [nguruvilu-c03], so natives avoided bathing in its lakes [nguruvilu-c05].

long_description.id: Nguruvilu dikatakan hidup di pusaran air berbahaya yang membunuh orang yang mencoba menyeberangi sungai, dan membuat air tampak dangkal agar penyeberangan terlihat aman [nguruvilu-c07]. Bagi orang awam, satu-satunya cara menyingkirkan nguruvilu adalah lewat machi atau kalku yang baik [nguruvilu-c09]; kalku menyelam ke pusaran dan menangkap makhluk itu dengan kemampuan sihirnya [nguruvilu-c10].
long_description.en: The nguruvilu is said to live in dangerous whirlpools that kill people trying to cross rivers, and it makes the water look shallow so that crossing seems safe [nguruvilu-c07]. Ordinary people can rid themselves of a nguruvilu only by calling on a machi or a kind-hearted kalku [nguruvilu-c09]; the kalku dives into the whirlpool and captures the creature with magical abilities [nguruvilu-c10].

long_description.id: Lehmann-Nitsche (1902) menulis bahwa, menurut informannya, ular-rubah dipercaya tidak mencelakai selama bentuk ibadah tertentu dijalankan [nguruvilu-c11]. Memanggil namanya langsung dianggap tabu dan sebutan "penguasa air" dipakai sebagai gantinya [nguruvilu-c12]. Wujudnya digambarkan berbeda-beda: berkepala rubah dan bertubuh ular, atau mirip kulit lembu yang menggembung [nguruvilu-c14], atau berkepala kucing dengan ekor panjang seperti rubah [nguruvilu-c15], atau berwajah puma atau kucing liar dengan ekor bercakar [nguruvilu-c08]; sebuah kamus mitologi menyebutnya setengah rubah setengah ular yang hidup di perairan berlumpur [nguruvilu-c16].
long_description.en: Lehmann-Nitsche (1902) wrote that, according to his informant, the fox-viper was believed to do no harm so long as a certain form of worship was performed [nguruvilu-c11]. It was taboo to call it by name and the phrase "lord of the water" was used instead [nguruvilu-c12]. Its form is described in different ways: fox-headed with a serpent's body, or like a bloated ox hide [nguruvilu-c14], or cat-headed with a long fox-like tail [nguruvilu-c15], or a puma-like or wildcat-like face with a tail bearing claws [nguruvilu-c08]; a mythology dictionary calls it half fox and half serpent living in muddy waters [nguruvilu-c16].

long_description.id: Antropolog Robert Lehmann-Nitsche berpendapat bahwa mitos ini berasal dari pengamatan terhadap berang-berang laut Lutra felina [nguruvilu-c13].
long_description.en: Anthropologist Robert Lehmann-Nitsche was of the opinion that the myth originated from observations of the marine otter Lutra felina [nguruvilu-c13].

cultural_context.id: Menurut informan yang dicatat Lehmann-Nitsche, ular-rubah tidak mencelakai selama ibadah tertentu dijalankan [nguruvilu-c11], dan menyebut namanya langsung dianggap tabu [nguruvilu-c12].
cultural_context.en: According to the informant recorded by Lehmann-Nitsche, the fox-viper did no harm so long as a certain worship was performed [nguruvilu-c11], and calling it by name was taboo [nguruvilu-c12].

text.en: Recorded in a commissioner's report of 1906

short_description.id: Ninki Nanka adalah makhluk legenda mirip naga dari cerita rakyat Gambia, yang dipercaya menghuni rawa dan hutan lebat serta membawa maut bagi siapa pun yang menatapnya.
short_description.en: The Ninki Nanka is a dragon-like legendary creature of the folklore of Gambia, believed to haunt swamps and dense bush and to bring death to anyone who meets its gaze.

long_description.id: Ninki Nanka dikenal dalam cerita rakyat orang Mandinka di Gambia. Banyak penduduk Gambia hilir konon menghindari rawa, sungai, bukit, dan anak sungai yang subur karena takut padanya. Ia dipercaya tinggal di hutan berawa dan gua, dan sering disebut naga sungai atau naga rawa.
long_description.en: The Ninki Nanka belongs to the folklore of the Mandinka of Gambia. Many people of the lower Gambia were said to shun fertile swamps, rivers, hills and creeks out of fear of it. It was believed to live in swampy forests and caves and is often called a river or swamp dragon.

long_description.id: Wujudnya berbeda menurut tiap suku, tetapi umumnya reptil. Ada yang menyebut kepala buaya pada tubuh keledai, ada yang menyebut campuran kuda nil dan jerapah, ada pula yang menganggapnya ular besar. Kisah lain melukiskan binatang rawa sepanjang 9 m bertubuh mirip buaya, bersisik bagai cermin, berleher jerapah, berkepala kuda, dan bertanduk tiga.
long_description.en: Its form varies from tribe to tribe, though most see it as a reptile. Some speak of a crocodile's head on a donkey's body, others of a hippopotamus-giraffe mix, others again of a large snake. Another account pictures a 9m marsh beast with a crocodile-like body, mirror-like scales, a giraffe's neck, a horse's head and three horns.

long_description.id: Ciri yang paling sering disebut adalah tatapannya yang mematikan, sehingga orang dianjurkan membawa cermin untuk menangkisnya. Sisiknya konon berkilau aneka warna sehingga ia bisa menyamar. Laporan komisaris tahun 1906 menyamakannya dengan ular raksasa bermahkota di semak paling lebat: melihat tubuhnya membawa penyakit, melihat mata atau mahkotanya berarti mati seketika.
long_description.en: The trait most often mentioned is its deadly stare, and people are advised to carry mirrors to turn it aside. Its scales are said to shimmer in many colours, letting it blend in. A 1906 commissioner's report compared it to a giant crowned serpent of the thickest bush: sighting its body brought illness, while sighting its eyes or crown meant sudden death.

long_description.id: Sebagai roh jahat, Ninki Nanka juga dipercaya mendatangkan kekeringan dan kelaparan. Di masa kini makhluk ini dibandingkan dengan monster Loch Ness, dan pada Juli 2006 Centre for Fortean Zoology mengirim ekspedisi ke Gambia untuk mencarinya.
long_description.en: As an evil spirit, the Ninki Nanka was also believed to cause drought and famine. Today it is compared with the Loch Ness monster, and in July 2006 the Centre for Fortean Zoology sent an expedition to Gambia to look for it.

claims.quote: A Ninki Nanka is a legendary creature in West African folklore.

statement.id: Ninki Nanka adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat (folklore).
statement.en: The Ninki Nanka is a legendary creature in folklore.

claims.quote: The Ninki Nanka kept many lower Gambians away from fertile swamps, rivers, hills, and creeks, and the creature was often believed to inhabit swampy forests and caves.

statement.id: Ninki Nanka membuat banyak orang di Gambia hilir menjauhi rawa, sungai, bukit, dan anak sungai yang subur; ia dipercaya menghuni hutan berawa dan gua (swampy forests and caves).
statement.en: The Ninki Nanka kept many people of the lower Gambia away from fertile swamps, rivers, hills and creeks; it was believed to inhabit swampy forests and caves.

claims.quote: Various accounts have also described it as a river or swamp dragon.

statement.id: Berbagai kisah menggambarkannya sebagai naga sungai atau naga rawa (river or swamp dragon).
statement.en: Various accounts describe it as a river or swamp dragon.

claims.quote: Descriptions of the creature vary across different tribes, but most contend that the animal is reptilian. It is depicted as having the head of a crocodile with the body of a donkey or a blend of hippopotamus and giraffe, and sometimes simply as a large snake.

statement.id: Gambarannya berbeda antarsuku, tetapi kebanyakan menyebutnya reptil: berkepala buaya dengan tubuh keledai atau campuran kuda nil dan jerapah (hippopotamus and giraffe), kadang sekadar ular besar.
statement.en: Descriptions differ between tribes, but most say it is reptilian: a crocodile's head on a donkey's body or a hippopotamus-giraffe blend, sometimes simply a large snake.

claims.quote: Some accounts of the legendary creature describe it as a 9m or 30-foot long marsh-dwelling beast having a body like that of a crocodile, mirror-like scales and long neck like that of a giraffe with a horse's head along with three horns.

statement.id: Sebagian kisah menyebutnya binatang rawa sepanjang 9 m (30-foot) bertubuh seperti buaya, bersisik seperti cermin, berleher panjang seperti jerapah, berkepala kuda, dan bertanduk tiga.
statement.en: Some accounts describe a 9m (30-foot) marsh-dwelling beast with a crocodile-like body, mirror-like scales, a giraffe-like long neck, a horse's head and three horns.

claims.quote: Common across descriptions is its believed fatal stare, akin to Medusa, which is said to cause death upon eye contact. Folklore advises carrying mirrors to deflect its gaze.

statement.id: Hampir semua kisah menyebut tatapannya mematikan (fatal stare), seperti Medusa; cerita rakyat menganjurkan membawa cermin untuk menangkis tatapannya.
statement.en: Most descriptions credit it with a fatal stare, akin to Medusa, causing death on eye contact; folklore advises carrying mirrors to deflect its gaze.

claims.quote: Another belief is that it has the ability to camouflage, using its scales which shimmer in various colors. ... The animal is said to be extremely large and very dangerous.

statement.id: Ia juga dipercaya mampu menyamarkan diri (camouflage) dengan sisik yang berkilau aneka warna, serta disebut sangat besar dan sangat berbahaya.
statement.en: It is also believed able to camouflage itself with scales that shimmer in various colours, and is said to be extremely large and very dangerous.

claims.quote: A 1906 commissioner's report describes the creature: ... this is supposed to resemble a gigantic crowned serpent which resides in the thickest bush. If a native sees the body of this creature he believes that he will be afflicted with dangerous sickness but that if he sees the eyes or crown it means instantaneous death.

statement.id: Laporan komisaris 1906 menyebutnya mirip ular raksasa bermahkota (crowned serpent) yang tinggal di semak paling lebat; melihat tubuhnya membawa penyakit berbahaya, melihat mata atau mahkotanya berarti kematian seketika.
statement.en: A 1906 commissioner's report likens it to a gigantic crowned serpent living in the thickest bush; seeing its body brings dangerous sickness, while seeing its eyes or crown means instant death.

text.id: Disebut dalam catatan tertulis awal sebagai kepercayaan Tagalog yang masih terdengar.
text.en: Mentioned in an early written account as a Tagalog belief still heard in the Philippines.

cultural_context.id: Kebiasaan mengucapkan tabi tabi po saat melewati gundukan dan meminta izin sebelum menebang pohon mencerminkan sikap hormat terhadap roh leluhur penghuni alam.
cultural_context.en: The habit of saying tabi tabi po when passing mounds and asking permission before felling trees reflects respect for ancestral spirits dwelling in nature.

who.id: Roh alam mirip kurcaci, kakek mungil penghuni gundukan tanah.
who.en: A dwarf-like nature spirit, a tiny old man of the mound.

origin.id: Mitologi Filipina, terutama kepercayaan Tagalog.
origin.en: Philippine mythology, especially Tagalog belief.

role.id: Roh leluhur yang harus dimintai izin dan dihormati.
role.en: An ancestral spirit whose permission must be asked and who must be respected.

famous_for.id: Ucapan tabi tabi po saat melewati gundukan dan kutukan bagi yang mengganggunya.
famous_for.en: Saying tabi tabi po when passing a mound, and the curses on those who disturb him.

did_you_know.id: Nama nono atau nuno, yang berarti kakek, juga pernah diberikan kepada buaya, dan dipercaya jiwa orang yang dimakan buaya tetap berada di dalam hewan itu.
did_you_know.en: The name nono or nuno, meaning grandfather, was also given to alligators, and it is believed that the soul of a person devoured by an alligator remains inside the animal.

description.id: Nuno dapat mengutuk penyusup dengan penyakit, bisul, bengkak, nyeri, muntah darah, atau bulu berlebihan di punggung; jika dalam jangkauan, ia dapat meludahi bagian tubuh mana pun.
description.en: A nuno can curse trespassers with illness, boils, swelling, pain, vomiting of blood or excessive back hair; if within range it can spit on any part of the body.

description.id: Nuno disebut mampu merasakan kebaikan dan kejahatan, mengenali orang yang memancarkan kemurnian, dan membuat sakit orang yang skeptis atau gelap agar menjauh.
description.en: Nunos are said to sense goodness and evil, to recognise those who radiate purity, and to make skeptical or dark people ill so they stay away.

description.id: Nuno membalas orang yang merusak atau mengganggu gundukannya, misalnya membuat kaki yang menendangnya bengkak, dan dalam catatan awal menghukum penyusup hutan dengan memelintir kepalanya ke belakang.
description.en: A nuno takes revenge on those who damage or disturb his mound, for example by making the foot that kicked it swell, and an early account says it punished forest intruders by twisting their heads backward.

description.id: Kutukan dapat diredakan dengan persembahan makanan atau meminta maaf langsung kepada nuno.
description.en: A curse can be lifted with food offerings or a direct apology to the nuno.

description.id: Nuno dapat dibunuh dengan menangkapnya dan meremukkan kepalanya di antara jari atau paha, yang menghapus mantranya, tetapi cara ini tidak dianjurkan.
description.en: A nuno can be killed by catching it and crushing its head between the fingers or thighs, removing its spell, but this is not recommended.

description.id: Ketika pedesaan menjadi modern, nuno sering melarikan diri, mati, atau pergi lebih dalam ke dalam tanah.
description.en: As the countryside modernises, nunos often flee, die, or go deeper into the earth.

description.id: Di Bulacan, nunó adalah kakek yang sangat tua yang tinggal di hutan, terutama di sarang semut atau gundukan apa pun, dan disebut juga Matandá sa punsó.
description.en: In Bulacan, nunó is a very old man who resides in forests, particularly in anthills or any mounds, also called Matandá sa punsó.

description.id: Orang Visayas menyebut pohon baliti Nonok dan percaya roh yang tinggal di dalamnya dapat mencelakai bila tidak ditakuti atau dihormati.
description.en: The Visayans call the baliti tree Nonok and believe the spirits dwelling in it may cause harm if not feared or respected.

description.id: Tempat nunó disebut sebagai kakek yang sangat tua penghuni hutan, terutama sarang semut atau gundukan.
description.en: Where the nunó is described as a very old man living in forests, particularly anthills or mounds.

description.id: Anito atau nono dipercaya tinggal terutama di pohon baliti (Ficus indica, L.).
description.en: The anitos or nonos are believed to reside particularly in baliti trees (Ficus indica, L.).

note.id: Maximo Ramos menggambarkan duwende sebagai roh ladang, roh bukit, dan orang tanah. Satu sumber membedakan nuno dari dwende yang suka bermain; sumber lain menyebut duwende umumnya digambarkan sebagai kakek atau nuno setinggi anak kecil, dan nuno sa punso biasanya sedikit lebih kecil daripada dwende rata-rata.
note.en: Maximo Ramos described duwende as spirits of the fields and hills and people of the ground. One source distinguishes the nuno from the playful dwende; another says duwende are commonly described as an old man or nuno with a small child's height, and the nuno sa punso is usually slightly smaller than the average dwende.

note.id: Orang Ilokano menyebut ansisit, kakek pendek yang tinggal di bawah tanah, gua, dan sarang semut; sumber ini tidak menyamakannya dengan nuno. Laporan dalam koleksi kepercayaan rakyat juga menggambarkan makhluk kecil pembalas yang menghukum setelah sarang semut dihancurkan.
note.en: The Ilokanos call the ansisit a short old man living underground, in caves and in anthills; the source does not equate it with the nuno. Reports in a folk-belief collection also describe retaliating little folk who punish after an ant hill is destroyed.

description.en: A romantic fantasy film in which the hero shrinks himself to save his love within the mounds where a nuno lives.

short_description.id: Nuno sa punso, atau kakek dari gundukan, adalah roh alam mirip kurcaci dalam mitologi Filipina yang dipercaya tinggal di sarang semut atau gundukan rayap dan mengutuk orang yang merusak atau mengganggu tempat tinggalnya.
short_description.en: The nuno sa punso, the old man of the mound, is a dwarf-like nature spirit of Philippine mythology believed to live in anthills or termite mounds and to curse those who damage or disturb his home.

long_description.id: Nuno sa punso, yang berarti kakek dari gundukan, atau cukup nuno, adalah roh alam mirip kurcaci dalam mitologi Filipina. Ia dipercaya tinggal di sarang semut atau gundukan rayap, tetapi juga di bawah batu besar, pohon, tepi sungai, gua, atau kebun. Nuno adalah roh leluhur: sebelum menebang pohon atau membuka tanah baru, orang meminta izin kepadanya agar tidak ditimpa malapetaka.
long_description.en: The nuno sa punso, meaning old man of the mound, or simply nuno, is a dwarf-like nature spirit of Philippine mythology. It is believed to live in anthills or termite mounds, but also under large rocks, trees, riverbanks, caves or gardens. The nuno are ancestral spirits: before felling a tree or breaking new ground, people ask their permission to avoid misfortune.

long_description.id: Sebuah catatan awal menyebut bahwa orang Tagalog menamai roh leluhur itu nuno, dan penyusup hutan yang tidak meminta persetujuan mereka dihukum dengan kepala dipelintir ke belakang. Menurut catatan lain, nono atau nuno, yang berarti kakek, awalnya nama bagi roh leluhur orang Tagalog kuno dan akhirnya bagi semua roh anito; nama yang sama juga diberikan kepada buaya. Di Bulacan, nunó digambarkan sebagai kakek yang sangat tua penghuni hutan, terutama sarang semut atau gundukan. Orang Tagalog menyebut kakek ini berusia sangat tua dan biasanya terlihat berjongkok di dalam gundukan.
long_description.en: An early account says the Tagalogs called these ancestral spirits nuno, and forest intruders who did not seek their consent were punished by having their heads twisted backward. According to another account, nono or nuno, meaning grandfather, was first a name for the spirits of the old Tagalogs' ancestors and ultimately for all anito spirits; the same name was also given to alligators. In Bulacan, the nunó is described as a very old man living in forests, particularly anthills or mounds. The Tagalogs say this old man was of great age and was usually seen crouching in a mound.

long_description.id: Nuno digambarkan sebagai kakek mungil yang berbeda dari dwende, makhluk jahil yang menampakkan diri kepada anak-anak. Nuno mudah marah dan membalas orang yang merusak atau mengganggu gundukannya, misalnya membuat kaki yang menendangnya membengkak. Kutukannya mencakup penyakit, bisul, bengkak atau nyeri, muntah darah, buang air kecil cairan hitam, dan bulu berlebihan di punggung.
long_description.en: The nuno is described as a tiny old man who differs from the dwende, a playful hobgoblin who shows himself to children. The nuno is easily angered and takes revenge on those who damage or disturb his mound, for example by making the foot that kicked it swell. His curses include illness, boils, swelling or pain, vomiting of blood, urinating black liquid, and excessive back hair.

long_description.id: Di Filipina umum dipercaya bahwa penyakit yang tak tersembuhkan obat modern mungkin akibat kutukan nuno. Korban dibawa ke albularyo, praktisi pengobatan tradisional, yang melakukan ramalan pagtatawas. Keluarga korban mungkin diminta memberi persembahan buah, makanan, minuman, atau benda kepada nuno, atau meminta maaf langsung kepadanya. Ada pula kepercayaan bahwa nuno dapat dibunuh dengan meremukkan kepalanya, tetapi cara itu tidak dianjurkan karena dapat memancing murka kerabatnya.
long_description.en: Filipinos commonly suspect that a sickness beyond modern medicine may come from a nuno. Such a patient is taken to an albularyo, a traditional-medicine practitioner, who performs the divination called pagtatawas. The victim's family may be asked to offer fruit, food, drink or an object to the nuno, or to ask its forgiveness in person. There is also a belief that a nuno can be killed by crushing its head, but this is not recommended as it could incur the wrath of its kin.

long_description.id: Untuk menghindari murka nuno, anak-anak diingatkan agar tidak bermain di luar antara tengah hari dan pukul tiga sore dan pulang sebelum pukul enam sore, serta meminta izin dengan mengucapkan tabi tabi po saat melewati tempat yang dihuni nuno. Orang tua di provinsi mengajarkan untuk selalu meminta permisi saat melewati gundukan tanah. Orang yang tidak hormat sengaja menginjak-injak rumput tinggi atau buang air kecil di sarang semut yang diduga milik nuno. Film fantasi Nuno sa Punso (1950) menampilkan tokoh yang mengecilkan diri di dalam gundukan tempat nuno tinggal.
long_description.en: To avoid the nuno's wrath, children are reminded not to play outside between noon and three in the afternoon and to come home before six in the evening, and to ask permission by saying tabi tabi po when passing places where the nuno dwell. Elders in the provinces taught people always to excuse themselves when passing an earth mound. Disrespectful people purposely trample tall grass or urinate on suspected nuno anthills. The fantasy film Nuno sa Punso (1950) shows a hero who shrinks himself within the mounds where a nuno lives.

claims.quote: The nuno are the spirits of the ancestors. When a tree is to be felled, or a piece of virgin ground broken, or on many other occasions, permission is asked of the nuno, in order to avoid the misfortune that would come from angering it.

statement.id: Nuno adalah roh leluhur; sebelum menebang pohon atau membuka tanah baru, orang meminta izin kepadanya agar terhindar dari malapetaka karena membuatnya marah.
statement.en: The nuno are ancestral spirits; before felling a tree or breaking new ground, people ask their permission to avoid the misfortune of angering them.

claims.quote: The nuno is described to be a tiny old man, but differs from a dwende or dwarf of Philippine folklore. The dwende is a playful hobgoblin who shows himself to children, while the nuno is a goblin easily angered that will do harm to those who damage or disturb his mound, and will seek retribution, for example by causing the foot of someone who kicked his mound to become swollen.

statement.id: Nuno digambarkan sebagai kakek mungil yang berbeda dari dwende, makhluk jahil yang menampakkan diri kepada anak-anak; nuno adalah goblin yang mudah marah, mencelakai orang yang merusak atau mengganggu gundukannya, dan membalas, misalnya dengan membuat kaki orang yang menendang gundukannya membengkak.
statement.en: The nuno is described as a tiny old man who differs from the dwende, a playful hobgoblin who shows himself to children; the nuno is an easily angered goblin who harms those who damage or disturb his mound and seeks retribution, for example by making swollen the foot of someone who kicked his mound.

claims.quote: Nunos have the ability to curse trespassers. A curse may include the following: Illness Boils Swelling or pain on any part of the body Vomiting of blood Urinating black liquid Excessive hair growth on the back

statement.id: Nuno dapat mengutuk penyusup; kutukannya antara lain penyakit, bisul, bengkak atau nyeri di bagian tubuh mana pun, muntah darah, buang air kecil cairan hitam, dan tumbuhnya bulu berlebihan di punggung.
statement.en: Nunos can curse trespassers; a curse may include illness, boils, swelling or pain on any part of the body, vomiting of blood, urinating black liquid, and excessive hair growth on the back.

claims.quote: It is a common belief in the Philippines that if modern medicine is unable to cure a particular illness, the ailment may be due to a nuno's curse. The victim is brought to an albularyo, a Philippine practitioner of traditional medicine. The albularyo will perform a type of divination known as pagtatawas.

statement.id: Di Filipina umum dipercaya bahwa penyakit yang tak tersembuhkan obat modern mungkin akibat kutukan nuno; korban dibawa ke albularyo, praktisi pengobatan tradisional Filipina, yang melakukan ramalan bernama pagtatawas.
statement.en: It is a common belief in the Philippines that if modern medicine cannot cure an illness, it may be due to a nuno's curse; the victim is brought to an albularyo, a Philippine practitioner of traditional medicine, who performs a divination known as pagtatawas.

claims.quote: In order to be cured, the victim's family may be asked to provide an offering to the nuno such as fruits or other food, drink, or a material object. If the victim is still sick after the offering, it may be necessary to personally ask the nuno's forgiveness

statement.id: Untuk sembuh, keluarga korban dapat diminta memberi persembahan buah, makanan, minuman, atau benda kepada nuno; bila masih sakit, perlu meminta maaf langsung kepadanya.
statement.en: To be cured, the victim's family may offer fruit, food, drink or an object to the nuno; if still ill, they may need to ask its forgiveness in person.

claims.quote: our elders instructed us always to excuse ourselves (thus the term “tabi tabi po” became a common phrase in our country) whenever we are passing by this soil formation

statement.id: Orang tua di provinsi Filipina mengajarkan untuk selalu meminta permisi (tabi tabi po) setiap kali melewati gundukan tanah.
statement.en: Elders in the Philippine provinces taught people always to excuse themselves (tabi tabi po) when passing an earth mound.

claims.quote: The late Dr. Maximo Ramos, one of the early scholars who created a compendium of lower mythological creatures of the Philippines, describe Dwarves or Duwende as a “spirit of the fields”, “spirit of the hills” and “people of the ground.”
claims.locator: Old man with a child's body

statement.id: Maximo Ramos menggambarkan kurcaci atau duwende sebagai 'roh ladang', 'roh bukit', dan 'orang tanah'.
statement.en: Maximo Ramos described dwarves or duwende as 'spirit of the fields', 'spirit of the hills' and 'people of the ground'.

claims.quote: Nuno sa punso are also believed to reside in places such as underneath large rocks, trees, riverbanks, caves, or a garden.

statement.id: Nuno sa punso juga dipercaya tinggal di tempat seperti di bawah batu besar, pohon, tepi sungai, gua, atau kebun.
statement.en: Nuno sa punso are also believed to reside in places such as underneath large rocks, trees, riverbanks, caves, or a garden.

claims.quote: In order for a nuno to successfully curse a person, the trespasser must be in close proximity to the nuno. If the trespasser is within range, the Nuno can spit on any part of the trespasser's body. The trespasser will then experience aches or soreness on the affected part of the body

statement.id: Agar kutukan berhasil, penyusup harus berada dekat dengan nuno; jika dalam jangkauan, nuno dapat meludahi bagian tubuh mana pun, dan penyusup lalu merasakan nyeri atau pegal di bagian itu.
statement.en: For a curse to succeed the trespasser must be close to the nuno; if within range the nuno can spit on any part of the trespasser's body, and the trespasser then feels aches or soreness there.

claims.quote: It is also possible to kill the nuno by catching it and crushing its head between a person's fingers or thighs. This will remove any spell cast by the nuno. But this method is often not recommended as it could incur the wrath of a nuno's kin and friends.

statement.id: Nuno dapat dibunuh dengan menangkapnya dan meremukkan kepalanya di antara jari atau paha, yang menghapus mantra yang dilontarkannya; cara ini tidak dianjurkan karena dapat memancing murka kerabat dan teman nuno.
statement.en: A nuno can be killed by catching it and crushing its head between the fingers or thighs, which removes any spell it cast; the method is often not recommended as it could incur the wrath of the nuno's kin and friends.

claims.quote: Nunos are protectors of the Earth, and have the ability to sense goodness and evil. If you radiate purity, they are able to tell, and will often reveal themselves. If you have skepticism, cynicism or darkness, they will avoid you or make you ill so you stay away from the area.

statement.id: Nuno disebut pelindung bumi yang mampu merasakan kebaikan dan kejahatan; orang yang memancarkan kemurnian akan mereka kenali dan sering mereka temui, sedangkan orang yang skeptis atau gelap dihindari atau dibuat sakit agar menjauh.
statement.en: Nunos are called protectors of the Earth able to sense goodness and evil; those who radiate purity are recognised and often met, while those with skepticism or darkness are avoided or made ill so they stay away.

claims.quote: When countryside becomes modernized and urbanized, the nunos often flee, die, or go further down into the earth.

statement.id: Ketika pedesaan menjadi modern dan perkotaan, nuno sering melarikan diri, mati, atau pergi lebih dalam ke dalam tanah.
statement.en: When the countryside becomes modernized and urbanized, the nunos often flee, die, or go further down into the earth.

claims.quote: To avoid the wrath of a nuno sa punso, children are reminded not to play outside between noon and three o'clock in the afternoon. They are also asked by their parents to come home before six o'clock in the evening.

statement.id: Untuk menghindari murka nuno sa punso, anak-anak diingatkan agar tidak bermain di luar antara tengah hari dan pukul tiga sore, dan diminta orang tua pulang sebelum pukul enam sore.
statement.en: To avoid the wrath of a nuno sa punso, children are reminded not to play outside between noon and three o'clock in the afternoon and are asked by their parents to come home before six in the evening.

claims.quote: Children are also warned to ask permission or give fair notice before passing by such places inhabited by the nuno, which is done by saying "tabi tabi po"(literally "please be on the side" or "please move aside", that is, you tell the nuno to stand aside)

statement.id: Anak-anak juga diperingatkan agar meminta izin atau memberi tahu sebelum melewati tempat yang dihuni nuno, yaitu dengan mengucapkan "tabi tabi po" (secara harfiah "mohon minggir"), yang berarti meminta nuno menepi.
statement.en: Children are also warned to ask permission or give notice before passing places inhabited by the nuno, by saying "tabi tabi po" (literally "please be on the side" or "please move aside"), that is, telling the nuno to stand aside.

claims.quote: A disrespectful person will purposely trample around in tall grassy areas, places where nuno are also believed to inhabit or will intentionally urinate on suspected nuno anthills to display dominance over the mound dweller.

statement.id: Orang yang tidak hormat sengaja menginjak-injak area rumput tinggi, tempat yang juga dipercaya dihuni nuno, atau sengaja buang air kecil di sarang semut yang diduga milik nuno untuk menunjukkan dominasi atas penghuni gundukan.
statement.en: A disrespectful person will purposely trample around in tall grassy areas, places where nuno are also believed to dwell, or intentionally urinate on suspected nuno anthills to display dominance over the mound dweller.

claims.quote: The 1950 romantic fantasy film Nuno sa Punso depicts a main hero reducing his size in order to save his love within the mounds where a nuno lives.

statement.id: Film fantasi romantis Nuno sa Punso (1950) menampilkan tokoh utama yang mengecilkan ukuran tubuhnya untuk menyelamatkan kekasihnya di dalam gundukan tempat nuno tinggal.
statement.en: The 1950 romantic fantasy film Nuno sa Punso depicts a main hero reducing his size in order to save his love within the mounds where a nuno lives.

claims.quote: Commonly described as an old man or ‘nuno’ with the height of a small child dwelling beneath the earth (thus the term “nuno sa punso”)

statement.id: Duwende umumnya digambarkan sebagai kakek atau "nuno" setinggi anak kecil yang tinggal di bawah tanah, sehingga muncul istilah "nuno sa punso".
statement.en: Duwende are commonly described as an old man or "nuno" with the height of a small child dwelling beneath the earth, hence the term "nuno sa punso".

claims.quote: Matanda sa punso — a Tagalog name referring to an old being associated with a mound.

statement.id: Matanda sa punso adalah nama Tagalog untuk makhluk tua yang dikaitkan dengan gundukan.
statement.en: Matanda sa punso is a Tagalog name referring to an old being associated with a mound.

claims.quote: Helpful or retaliating little folk — separate reports describe aid to poor or vulnerable people and punishment after an ant hill is destroyed (entries 4189–4191).
claims.locator: Regional Little-Folk Names in the Demetrio Collection

statement.id: Laporan-laporan terpisah dalam sebuah koleksi kepercayaan rakyat menggambarkan makhluk kecil penolong atau pembalas, termasuk hukuman setelah sarang semut dihancurkan.
statement.en: Separate reports in a folk-belief collection describe helpful or retaliating little folk, including punishment after an ant hill is destroyed.

claims.quote: NONO or NUNO – (Tagalogs) Meaning grandfather, was one of the names given by the old Tagalogs to the spirits of their ancestors and ultimately, to all anito spirits.

statement.id: Nono atau nuno (Tagalog), yang berarti kakek, adalah salah satu nama yang diberikan orang Tagalog kuno kepada roh leluhur mereka dan akhirnya kepada semua roh anito.
statement.en: Nono or nuno (Tagalog), meaning grandfather, was one of the names the old Tagalogs gave to the spirits of their ancestors and ultimately to all anito spirits.

claims.quote: The same name was given to alligators. It is believed that when an alligator devours a human, the soul remains inside the animal.

statement.id: Nama yang sama juga diberikan kepada buaya; dipercaya bahwa ketika buaya melahap manusia, jiwanya tetap berada di dalam hewan itu.
statement.en: The same name was also given to alligators; it is believed that when an alligator devours a human, the soul remains inside the animal.

claims.quote: It is also believed that the anitos or nonos reside particularly in baliti trees (Ficus indica, L.) thus it was given the name Nonok.

statement.id: Juga dipercaya bahwa anito atau nono tinggal terutama di pohon baliti (Ficus indica, L.), sehingga pohon itu dinamai Nonok.
statement.en: It is also believed that the anitos or nonos reside particularly in baliti trees (Ficus indica, L.), thus the tree was given the name Nonok.

claims.quote: The Tagalog peasants still believe in nunó. In Bulacan, nunó is a very old man who resides in forests particularly in the anthills or any mounds. Also called Matandá sa punsó.

statement.id: Petani Tagalog masih percaya pada nunó; di Bulacan, nunó adalah kakek yang sangat tua yang tinggal di hutan, terutama di sarang semut atau gundukan apa pun, dan disebut juga Matandá sa punsó.
statement.en: The Tagalog peasants still believe in nunó; in Bulacan, nunó is a very old man who resides in forests, particularly in anthills or any mounds, and is also called Matandá sa punsó.

claims.quote: Lastly, the Visayans also call the baliti tree Nonok and believe that the spirits who dwell in it may cause harm if they are not feared or respected.

statement.id: Orang Visayas juga menyebut pohon baliti Nonok dan percaya roh yang tinggal di dalamnya dapat mencelakai bila tidak ditakuti atau dihormati.
statement.en: The Visayans also call the baliti tree Nonok and believe that the spirits dwelling in it may cause harm if they are not feared or respected.

claims.quote: NUNO SA PUNSO – (Tagalogs) Nuno sa punso (literally, grandfather of the mound) are also simply called nuno. It lives inside a mound of earth, sometimes mistaken to be termites’ home, usually seen to be slightly smaller than the average dwende.

statement.id: Nuno sa punso (harfiah: kakek dari gundukan) juga disebut nuno saja; ia tinggal di dalam gundukan tanah yang kadang disangka rumah rayap, biasanya terlihat sedikit lebih kecil daripada dwende rata-rata.
statement.en: The nuno sa punso (literally grandfather of the mound) is also simply called nuno; it lives inside a mound of earth, sometimes mistaken for a termites' home, usually seen as slightly smaller than the average dwende.

claims.quote: The Ilokanos call him ansisit. He is an old man who is as short as a boy of three. His joints, belly, head, eyes, nose, and mouth are large. He lives underground and owns all the land. He lives in caves and anthills, too.

statement.id: Orang Ilokano menyebutnya ansisit: seorang kakek sependek anak tiga tahun, bersendi, perut, kepala, mata, hidung, dan mulut besar, yang tinggal di bawah tanah dan memiliki semua tanah, serta tinggal di gua dan sarang semut.
statement.en: The Ilokanos call him ansisit: an old man as short as a boy of three, with large joints, belly, head, eyes, nose and mouth, who lives underground and owns all the land, and also lives in caves and anthills.

claims.quote: Among the Tagologs they are called nuno, or ancestral spirits, and before entering woods their con- sent had to be asked, failing which the intruder was punished by having his head twisted so that his face looked backward.

statement.id: Di antara orang Tagalog, mereka disebut nuno, atau roh leluhur, dan sebelum memasuki hutan harus meminta persetujuan mereka; penyusup yang tidak melakukannya dihukum dengan kepala dipelintir sehingga wajahnya menghadap ke belakang.
statement.en: Among the Tagalogs they are called nuno, or ancestral spirits, and before entering woods their consent had to be asked; an intruder who failed to do so was punished by having his head twisted so that his face looked backward.

claims.quote: The nunos lived in mounds, which were made by the Anay called ... from which is derived “Matanda sa punso,” or “old man of the mounds,” still heard in the Philippines.

statement.id: Para nuno tinggal di gundukan yang dibuat oleh anay yang disebut punso, yang darinya diturunkan "Matanda sa punso" atau "kakek gundukan", yang masih terdengar di Filipina.
statement.en: The nunos lived in mounds made by the termites called punso, from which "Matanda sa punso", or "old man of the mounds", is derived, still heard in the Philippines.

claims.quote: The Tagologs say that this fantastic old man was of the most vener- able age, and was usually seen crouching in a mound.

statement.id: Orang Tagalog mengatakan bahwa kakek fantastis ini berusia sangat tua dan biasanya terlihat berjongkok di dalam gundukan.
statement.en: The Tagalogs say that this fantastic old man was of the most vener- able age and was usually seen crouching in a mound.

cultural_context.id: Legenda Seri Pahang menghubungkan buaya keramat Tasik Chini dengan penguasa Pahang, yang leluhurnya memakamkan Seri Pahang dengan layak; menurut kisah tahun 1914, buaya dan ikan memberi hormat pada pemakaman Sultan Ahmad sebagai tanda terima kasih.
cultural_context.en: The Seri Pahang legend links the sacred crocodile of Chini Lake with the rulers of Pahang, whose ancestor buried Seri Pahang properly; in the 1914 account the crocodiles and fish paid respects at Sultan Ahmad's funeral in gratitude.

who.id: Buaya putih raksasa penjaga Tasik Chini.
who.en: A giant white crocodile of Chini Lake.

origin.id: Cerita rakyat Melayu Pahang.
origin.en: Pahang Malay folklore.

role.id: Pelindung yang membunuh iblis laut Seri Kemboja.
role.en: A protector who killed the sea demon Seri Kemboja.

did_you_know.id: Ketika Seri Pahang sekarat di Sekukoh, perahu para pelaut tidak bisa bergerak sebelum kabarnya disampaikan di muara Sungai Chini.
did_you_know.en: When Seri Pahang lay dying at Sekukoh, the sailors' boat could not move until the news was delivered at the mouth of the Chini River.

description.id: Menjelma lelaki tua dan kembali menjadi buaya putih; kunyit di timbanya berubah menjadi emas.
description.en: Turns into an old man and back into a white crocodile; the turmeric in his pail turns to gold.

description.id: Dalam versi lain Seri Pahang dan Seri Kemboja digambarkan sebagai naga; Mythlok menyebut Seri Pahang naga bersisik perak.
description.en: In another version Seri Pahang and Seri Kemboja are described as naga; Mythlok calls Seri Pahang a silver-scaled naga.

role.id: Pahlawan yang membunuh iblis laut
role.en: The hero who kills the sea demon

summary.id: Menyamar sebagai lelaki tua, Seri Pahang menumpang kapal ke tempat pertempuran, berubah menjadi buaya putih, dan membunuh Seri Kemboja; ia kembali dalam keadaan terluka dan dimakamkan di Sekukoh.
summary.en: Disguised as an old man, Seri Pahang rides a ship to the battle site, becomes a white crocodile and kills Seri Kemboja; he returns wounded and is buried at Sekukoh.

description.id: Danau air tawar alami terbesar kedua di Malaysia yang dianggap keramat bersama gunung di sampingnya; tempat tinggal Seri Pahang dalam cerita.
description.en: The second largest natural freshwater lake in Malaysia, held sacred together with its adjoining mountain; Seri Pahang's home in the tale.

description.id: Tempat Seri Pahang dimakamkan di lubang berpasir dekat Sekukoh di Sungai Pahang.
description.en: Where Seri Pahang was buried in a sandy pit near Sekukoh on the Pahang River.

description.id: Titik di tenggaranya tempat Seri Pahang melompat ke laut menjadi buaya putih.
description.en: The spot southeast of it where Seri Pahang leapt into the sea as a white crocodile.

description.id: Pulau tempat Seri Pahang berenang setelah terluka lalu kembali menjadi lelaki tua.
description.en: The island he swam to when wounded, where he became an old man again.

description.id: Dua puluh enam buaya terlihat berenang ke hulu di Sungai Pahang; orang percaya mereka pulang dari pemakaman sultan.
description.en: Twenty-six crocodiles were seen heading upriver on the Pahang River; people believed they were returning from the sultan's funeral.

note.en: The black sea demon Seri Pahang killed in this legend.

short_description.id: Seri Pahang adalah buaya muara putih raksasa dalam cerita rakyat Melayu Pahang yang konon tinggal di Tasik Chini dan terkenal karena bertarung melawan iblis laut hitam Seri Kemboja.
short_description.en: Seri Pahang is a legendary giant white saltwater crocodile of Pahang Malay folklore said to live in Chini Lake, famous for its duel with the black sea demon Seri Kemboja.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Melayu Pahang, Seri Pahang adalah buaya muara putih raksasa yang konon hidup di Tasik Chini, Distrik Pekan, Pahang. Ia terkenal karena duelnya dengan iblis laut hitam bernama Seri Kemboja di lepas pantai Pahang. Dalam versi lain keduanya digambarkan sebagai ular raksasa yang disebut naga. Menurut kisah setempat, danau dan gunung di sampingnya keramat, dan penduduk menganggap tempat itu memiliki buaya putih yang dijuluki 'Seri Pahang', 'kemuliaan Pahang'.
long_description.en: In Pahang Malay folklore Seri Pahang is a giant white saltwater crocodile said to have lived in Chini Lake, Pekan District, Pahang. He is known for his duel with a black sea demon named Seri Kemboja off the coast of Pahang. In another version both are described as giant serpents called naga. In local accounts the lake and the mountain beside it are sacred, and the place is credited with a white crocodile styled 'Seri Pahang', 'glory of Pahang'.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, kabar tentang iblis laut Seri Kemboja sampai kepada Seri Pahang dan ia bersumpah menyingkirkannya. Ia berenang ke Kuala Pahang, menjelma lelaki tua membawa timba dari palem, dan membujuk para pelaut membawanya serta. Di titik tenggara Sedili Kechil ia menyerahkan timba kepada nakhoda dan melompat ke laut; ia segera menjadi buaya putih raksasa, dan kunyit di timba itu menjadi emas, upah para pelaut.
long_description.en: According to the legend, word of the sea demon Seri Kemboja reached Seri Pahang and he vowed to remove him. He swam to Kuala Pahang, took the form of an old man carrying a bailing pail made of palm, and persuaded sailors to take him aboard. At a spot southeast of Sedili Kechil he gave the pail to the nakhoda and leapt into the sea; he at once became a giant white crocodile, and the turmeric in the pail turned to gold, the sailors' payment.

long_description.id: Pertarungan berlangsung lama; laut menjadi gelap, guruh bergemuruh, dan kilat menyambar. Seri Pahang berhasil membunuh Seri Kemboja tetapi terluka parah. Ia berenang ke Pulau Aur, kembali menjadi lelaki tua, dan menumpang perahu ke Kuala Pahang. Di Sekukoh ia makin lemah, meminta pelaut berhenti di muara Sungai Chini, dan mengumumkan bahwa ia sekarat; perahu baru dapat bergerak setelah kabar itu disampaikan, dan ratusan buaya terlihat berenang ke hilir menuju Sekukoh.
long_description.en: The fight lasted long; the sea turned dark, thunder rolled and lightning flashed. Seri Pahang killed Seri Kemboja but was badly wounded. He swam to Aur Island, became an old man again and got a boat ride to Kuala Pahang. At Sekukoh he grew weaker and had the sailors halt where the Chini River meets the Pahang, declaring that he was dying; hundreds of crocodiles were then seen swimming downriver to Sekukoh.

long_description.id: Sebelum mati, buaya putih itu meminta penguasa Pahang memberinya pemakaman keagamaan yang layak, dan setelah mengetahui bagaimana ia membunuh iblis laut, sang penguasa setuju. Seri Pahang dimakamkan di lubang berpasir dekat Sekukoh, tempat yang hingga kini dikenal sebagai Makam Tok Pahang. Pada 1914, ketika Sultan Ahmad wafat, orang melihat dua puluh enam buaya berenang ke hulu di Sungai Pahang dalam formasi "V", diikuti kawanan ikan; orang percaya mereka pulang dari pemakaman sultan sebagai tanda terima kasih.
long_description.en: Before dying, the white crocodile asked the ruler of Pahang for a proper religious burial, and after learning how he had killed the sea demon the ruler agreed. Seri Pahang was buried in a sandy pit near Sekukoh, a place known to this day as Makam Tok Pahang. In 1914, when Sultan Ahmad died, people saw twenty-six crocodiles heading upriver on the Pahang River in a "V" formation, followed by a shoal of fish; people believed they were returning from the sultan's funeral in gratitude.

long_description.id: Sumber lain menggambarkan Seri Pahang secara berbeda. Mythlok menyebutnya naga bersisik perak, satu dari lima naga bersaudara bersama Seri Daik, Seri Kemboja, Seri Siam, dan Seri Gumum. Sinar Harian (2021) mencatat bahwa Tasik Chini dikenal lewat legenda tiga naga yang dikatakan pernah menghuninya, yakni Seri Gumum, Seri Pahang, dan Seri Daik. TheSmartLocal menyebut "Nessie" Malaysia bernama Naga Seri Gumum, atau Seri Pahang, sedangkan Seri Kemboja disebut pasangan Seri Gumum dalam kisah lain.
long_description.en: Other sources picture Seri Pahang differently. Mythlok calls him a silver-scaled naga, one of five dragon siblings with Seri Daik, Seri Kemboja, Seri Siam and Seri Gumum. Sinar Harian (2021) notes that Chini Lake is famous for the legend of the nagas Seri Gumum, Seri Pahang and Seri Daik. TheSmartLocal says Malaysia's own Nessie is the Seri Gumum Dragon, or Seri Pahang, while Seri Kemboja is called Seri Gumum's consort in another tale.

claims.quote: In Pahang Malay folklore, Seri Pahang (Jawi: سري ڤهڠ) was a legendary giant white saltwater crocodile thought to have lived in the Chini Lake, Pekan District, Pahang. He was famous for his duel with a black sea demon called Seri Kemboja that took place off the coast of Pahang.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Melayu Pahang, Seri Pahang adalah buaya muara putih raksasa yang konon hidup di Tasik Chini, Distrik Pekan, Pahang, dan terkenal karena duelnya dengan iblis laut hitam bernama Seri Kemboja di lepas pantai Pahang.
statement.en: In Pahang Malay folklore, Seri Pahang (سري ڤهڠ) was a legendary giant white saltwater crocodile thought to have lived in Chini Lake, Pekan District, Pahang, famous for his duel with a black sea demon called Seri Kemboja off the coast of Pahang.

claims.quote: In the local lore, the lake and its adjoining mountain are sacred, and locals credit the place with the possession of a white crocodile styled 'Seri Pahang' (Malay for 'glory of Pahang').

statement.id: Dalam kisah setempat, danau dan gunung di sampingnya keramat, dan penduduk menganggap tempat itu memiliki buaya putih yang dijuluki 'Seri Pahang' (bahasa Melayu untuk 'kemuliaan Pahang').
statement.en: In the local lore the lake and its adjoining mountain are sacred, and locals credit the place with a white crocodile styled 'Seri Pahang' (Malay for 'glory of Pahang').

claims.quote: So Seri Pahang left Tasik Chini and swam downstream to Kuala Pahang. There he transformed into an old man carrying a bailing pail made of palm.

statement.id: Seri Pahang meninggalkan Tasik Chini, berenang ke Kuala Pahang, lalu menjelma lelaki tua membawa timba dari daun palem dan menumpang kapal para pelaut.
statement.en: Seri Pahang left Chini Lake, swam to Kuala Pahang and turned into an old man with a palm bailing pail, getting a ride with sailors.

claims.quote: He immediately turned into a giant white crocodile and the men were amazed to see that the turmeric in the dipper had turned to gold.

statement.id: Seri Pahang segera berubah menjadi buaya putih raksasa dan para pelaut takjub melihat kunyit di dalam timba telah menjadi emas.
statement.en: He immediately turned into a giant white crocodile and the men were amazed to see that the turmeric in the dipper had turned to gold.

claims.quote: That is how Seri Pahang came to be buried in a sandy pit near Sekukoh. The place is known to this day as Makam Tok Pahang ('Tok Pahang's Tomb').

statement.id: Seri Pahang dimakamkan di lubang berpasir dekat Sekukoh; tempat itu hingga kini dikenal sebagai Makam Tok Pahang ('Makam Tok Pahang').
statement.en: Seri Pahang came to be buried in a sandy pit near Sekukoh; the place is known to this day as Makam Tok Pahang ('Tok Pahang's Tomb').

claims.quote: In 1914, when Sultan Ahmad died, people saw twenty six crocodiles cruising in a “V” formation in Pahang River, heading upriver.

statement.id: Pada 1914, ketika Sultan Ahmad wafat, orang melihat dua puluh enam buaya berenang dalam formasi "V" di Sungai Pahang menuju hulu.
statement.en: In 1914, when Sultan Ahmad died, people saw twenty six crocodiles cruising in a "V" formation in the Pahang River, heading upriver.

claims.quote: In another version of the legend, both Seri Pahang and Seri Kemboja, are described as giant serpents called Nāga.

statement.id: Dalam versi lain legenda ini, Seri Pahang dan Seri Kemboja sama-sama digambarkan sebagai ular raksasa yang disebut naga.
statement.en: In another version of the legend, both Seri Pahang and Seri Kemboja are described as giant serpents called naga.

claims.quote: According to the legend, news had reached Seri Pahang about a devastating black sea demon, Seri Kemboja (the Glory of Kemboja). He vowed to fight the demon and get rid of him.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, kabar sampai kepada Seri Pahang tentang iblis laut hitam yang merusak, Seri Kemboja ("Kemuliaan Kemboja"); ia bersumpah melawan dan menyingkirkannya.
statement.en: According to the legend, news reached Seri Pahang of a devastating black sea demon, Seri Kemboja ("the Glory of Kemboja"); he vowed to fight and get rid of him.

claims.quote: In the form of the old man, Seri Pahang persuaded a group of sailors to take him on board with them. Since he had a bailing pail, they thought he might be useful if the boat needed to be bailed.

statement.id: Dalam wujud lelaki tua, Seri Pahang membujuk sekelompok pelaut agar membawanya serta; karena ia membawa timba, mereka mengira ia berguna bila perahu perlu dikuras.
statement.en: In the form of the old man, Seri Pahang persuaded a group of sailors to take him aboard; since he had a bailing pail they thought he might be useful if the boat needed bailing.

claims.quote: When the boat reached a spot southeast of Sedili Kechil, Seri Pahang handed the bailing pail to the nakhuda and jumped into the sea.

statement.id: Ketika perahu tiba di titik tenggara Sedili Kechil, Seri Pahang menyerahkan timba kepada nakhoda dan melompat ke laut.
statement.en: When the boat reached a spot southeast of Sedili Kechil, Seri Pahang handed the bailing pail to the nakhoda and jumped into the sea.

claims.quote: This was their payment for giving Seri Pahang a ride to the spot where he wanted to challenge Seri Kemboja, the black demon.

statement.id: Emas itu menjadi upah para pelaut karena telah membawa Seri Pahang ke tempat ia hendak menantang Seri Kemboja, iblis hitam itu.
statement.en: The gold was the sailors' payment for giving Seri Pahang a ride to the spot where he wanted to challenge Seri Kemboja, the black demon.

claims.quote: The fight between Seri Pahang and Seri Kemboja lasted long. The sea became dark, thunder rolled and lightning flashed. After a fierce battle, Seri Pahang managed to kill Seri Kemboja but he was wounded badly himself.

statement.id: Pertarungan itu berlangsung lama: laut menjadi gelap, guruh bergemuruh, dan kilat menyambar; setelah pertempuran sengit Seri Pahang berhasil membunuh Seri Kemboja tetapi sendiri terluka parah.
statement.en: The fight lasted long: the sea turned dark, thunder rolled and lightning flashed; after a fierce battle Seri Pahang killed Seri Kemboja but was himself badly wounded.

claims.quote: In great pain, he swam away to Aur Island, transformed himself back into an old man and got a boat ride back to Kuala Pahang.

statement.id: Dalam kesakitan, ia berenang ke Pulau Aur, kembali menjadi lelaki tua, dan menumpang perahu pulang ke Kuala Pahang.
statement.en: In great pain he swam to Aur Island, changed back into an old man and got a boat ride back to Kuala Pahang.

claims.quote: Once he reached a village called Sekukoh on the Pahang River, he was getting a very weak, and told the sailors to stop at the mouth of the Chini River and made announcement that he is dying at Sekukoh.

statement.id: Setibanya di desa Sekukoh di Sungai Pahang ia makin lemah, menyuruh pelaut berhenti di muara Sungai Chini, dan mengumumkan bahwa ia sekarat di Sekukoh.
statement.en: On reaching the village of Sekukoh on the Pahang River he grew very weak, told the sailors to stop at the mouth of the Chini River and announced that he was dying at Sekukoh.

claims.quote: Before long, hundreds of crocodiles could be seen swimming downriver to Sekukoh. There were so many crocodiles in the river that, villagers living along the banks claimed that daring young men could cross the river on backs of the crocodiles.

statement.id: Tak lama kemudian ratusan buaya terlihat berenang ke hilir menuju Sekukoh, begitu banyak sehingga warga mengatakan pemuda berani dapat menyeberangi sungai di atas punggung buaya.
statement.en: Before long hundreds of crocodiles were seen swimming downriver to Sekukoh, so many that villagers said daring young men could cross the river on their backs.

claims.quote: Before he died, the great white crocodile, asked the ruler of Pahang to give him a proper religious burial. After learning how the crocodile had killed the sea demon, the ruler agreed.

statement.id: Sebelum mati, buaya putih besar itu meminta penguasa Pahang memberinya pemakaman keagamaan yang layak; setelah mengetahui bagaimana buaya itu membunuh iblis laut, sang penguasa setuju.
statement.en: Before dying the great white crocodile asked the ruler of Pahang for a proper religious burial; after learning how the crocodile had killed the sea demon, the ruler agreed.

claims.quote: The people believed that the crocodiles and fish were coming back from the funeral of Sultan Ahmad. They had been paying their respects in gratitude, because the Sultan's ancestor had buried Seri Pahang properly at Sekukoh before he died.

statement.id: Orang percaya buaya dan ikan itu pulang dari pemakaman Sultan Ahmad; mereka memberi penghormatan sebagai tanda terima kasih karena leluhur sultan pernah memakamkan Seri Pahang dengan layak di Sekukoh.
statement.en: People believed the crocodiles and fish were returning from Sultan Ahmad's funeral, paying respects in gratitude because the sultan's ancestor had properly buried Seri Pahang at Sekukoh.

claims.quote: Behind them came a shoal of fish fanned out across the river. The people cast nets, but the fish magically escaped.

statement.id: Di belakang buaya-buaya itu datang kawanan ikan yang menyebar di sungai; orang menebar jala tetapi ikan itu lolos secara ajaib.
statement.en: Behind the crocodiles came a shoal of fish fanned out across the river; people cast nets but the fish escaped magically.

claims.quote: Chini Lake is the second largest natural freshwater lake in Malaysia. The Chini River, which drains from the lake, flows into the Pahang River.

statement.id: Tasik Chini adalah danau air tawar alami terbesar kedua di Malaysia; Sungai Chini yang mengalir dari danau itu bermuara ke Sungai Pahang.
statement.en: Chini Lake is the second largest natural freshwater lake in Malaysia; the Chini River, which drains from it, flows into the Pahang River.

claims.quote: It is one of five mythical dragon siblings, each associated with a different region and elemental color. The naga family includes Seri Daik (golden-scaled), Seri Pahang (silver-scaled), Seri Kemboja (copper or bronze-scaled), Seri Siam (with dull or ordinary scales), and Seri Gumum (iron-scaled), who inhabits Lake Chini.

statement.id: Mythlok menyebut naga Tasik Chini sebagai satu dari lima naga bersaudara: Seri Daik (bersisik emas), Seri Pahang (bersisik perak), Seri Kemboja (bersisik tembaga atau perunggu), Seri Siam, dan Seri Gumum (bersisik besi) yang mendiami Tasik Chini.
statement.en: Mythlok presents the Chini Lake naga as one of five dragon siblings: Seri Daik (golden-scaled), Seri Pahang (silver-scaled), Seri Kemboja (copper or bronze-scaled), Seri Siam and Seri Gumum (iron-scaled), who inhabits Lake Chini.

claims.quote: One tale recounts how a royal couple was cursed and transformed into naga—Seri Gumum and her consort Seri Kemboja—explaining both their guardianship of the lake and their supernatural bond.

statement.id: Menurut Mythlok, satu kisah menceritakan pasangan bangsawan yang dikutuk menjadi naga, Seri Gumum dan pasangannya Seri Kemboja, menjelaskan penjagaan mereka atas danau dan ikatan gaib keduanya.
statement.en: According to Mythlok, one tale recounts a royal couple cursed into naga, Seri Gumum and her consort Seri Kemboja, explaining their guardianship of the lake and their supernatural bond.

claims.quote: TASIK Chini yang terletak di Pahang terkenal dengan legenda Naga Seri Gumum, Naga Seri Pahang dan Naga Seri Daik yang dikatakan pernah menghuninya.

statement.id: Sinar Harian (2021) menyebut Tasik Chini di Pahang terkenal dengan legenda Naga Seri Gumum, Naga Seri Pahang, dan Naga Seri Daik yang dikatakan pernah menghuninya.
statement.en: Sinar Harian (2021) says Chini Lake in Pahang is famous for the legend of the nagas Seri Gumum, Seri Pahang and Seri Daik, said to have once lived there.

claims.quote: Malaysia has a Nessie of its own called Seri Gumum Dragon, or Seri Pahang.

statement.id: TheSmartLocal menyebut "Nessie" Malaysia sendiri bernama Naga Seri Gumum, atau Seri Pahang.
statement.en: TheSmartLocal says Malaysia has a Nessie of its own called the Seri Gumum Dragon, or Seri Pahang.

claims.quote: another recounts a love story between the female Seri Gumum and a male Nāga called Seri Kemboja that leads to the origin myth of Tioman and Lingga Islands

statement.id: Dalam artikel Seri Gumum, satu legenda lain menceritakan kisah cinta antara Seri Gumum (betina) dan naga jantan bernama Seri Kemboja yang melahirkan mitos asal Pulau Tioman dan Lingga.
statement.en: In the Seri Gumum article, another legend recounts a love story between the female Seri Gumum and a male naga called Seri Kemboja that leads to the origin myth of Tioman and Lingga Islands.

short_description.id: Shadow person adalah sosok dalam keyakinan paranormal yang menyerupai bayangan manusia hidup, kadang dianggap roh.
short_description.en: A shadow person is a paranormal belief figure resembling a living human shadow, sometimes interpreted as a spirit.

long_description.id: Shadow person adalah sosok dalam keyakinan paranormal yang menyerupai bayangan manusia hidup, kadang dianggap roh. Acara radio Coast to Coast AM membantu memopulerkan keyakinan modern tentang shadow people.
long_description.en: A shadow person is a paranormal belief figure resembling a living human shadow, sometimes interpreted as a spirit. Coast to Coast AM helps popularize modern beliefs about shadow people.

long_description.id: Heidi Hollis menerbitkan buku pertamanya tentang shadow people. Hollis menggambarkan shadow people sebagai siluet gelap yang berkedip pada penglihatan tepi. Penganut dan penulis paranormal berbeda pendapat apakah shadow people jahat, membantu, atau netral. Hat Man merupakan varian bernama demikian karena topi bertepi yang digambarkan di kepalanya.
long_description.en: Heidi Hollis publishes her first book about shadow people. Hollis describes shadow people as dark human silhouettes flickering in peripheral vision. Believers and paranormal authors disagree over whether shadow people are evil, helpful, or neutral. Hat Man is a variant named for the brimmed hat depicted on its head.

long_description.id: Dalam laporan yang dikutip sebuah ulasan skeptis, sosok ini paling sering berupa seorang pria yang mungkin bertopi atau berkerudung, dan sering hanya terlihat sekilas dari sudut mata. Laporan lain menggambarkan penampakan hitam pekat berbadan utuh dengan mata kosong yang menusuk. Cerita rakyat tentang makhluk berbayang juga sudah lama ada, misalnya Jin dalam Islam dan Nalusa Falaya suku Choctaw.
long_description.en: In reports quoted by a skeptical review, the figure is most often a man who may wear a hat or hood and is often glimpsed only at the corner of the eye. Other reports describe a full-bodied jet-black apparition with piercing empty eyes. Folklore about shadowy beings is also long established, for example the Islamic Jinn and the Choctaw Nalusa Falaya.

long_description.id: Beberapa kondisi fisiologis dan psikologis dipakai untuk menjelaskan pengalaman ini. Penderita lumpuh tidur dapat merasakan bentuk berbayang mendekat, dan banyak pecandu metamfetamin melaporkan shadow people setelah lama kurang tidur. Ulasan skeptis juga menyebut salah mengenali bayangan nyata, ilusi optik, halusinasi hipnagogik, dan sekadar mengarang cerita. Penggemar paranormal mengajukan penjelasan lain, termasuk proyeksi astral, sedangkan Hollis meyakininya sebagai alien negatif.
long_description.en: Several physiological and psychological conditions are used to explain these experiences. Sleep paralysis sufferers may sense a shadowy shape approaching, and many methamphetamine addicts report shadow people after long sleep deprivation. The skeptical review also names misidentified real shadows, optical illusions, hypnagogic hallucinations, and simple invention. Paranormal enthusiasts offer other explanations, including astral projection, while Hollis believes them to be negative aliens.

long_description.id: Hat Man ditampilkan sebagai siluet tinggi pria bertopi bertepi yang muncul di antara tidur dan sadar. Sejak akhir 2000-an orang membagikan kisah penglihatan yang sangat konsisten itu. Di internet ia sering disebut sebagai halusinasi akibat penyalahgunaan difenhidramin, sementara sebagian pembuat konten TikTok mengklaimnya shadow person yang nyata dan berpotensi jahat.
long_description.en: The Hat Man is presented as the tall silhouette of a man in a brimmed hat who appears between sleep and wakefulness. Since the late 2000s people have shared remarkably consistent stories of this vision. Online he is often cited as a hallucination from diphenhydramine abuse, while some TikTok creators claim he is a real and potentially evil shadow person.

cultural_context.id: Uraian ini mencatat keyakinan paranormal modern dan perbedaan tafsir para penganutnya.
cultural_context.en: This account records modern paranormal beliefs and differences among believers’ interpretations.

description.id: Hat Man berciri umum shadow people tetapi dinamai dari topi fedora atau topi bertepi lain di kepalanya. Sejak akhir 2000-an orang menceritakan penglihatan yang konsisten tentang siluet pria bertopi bertepi yang muncul antara tidur dan sadar; di internet ia sering disebut sebagai halusinasi akibat penyalahgunaan difenhidramin.
description.en: The Hat Man shares the general characteristics of shadow people but is named for a fedora or other brimmed hat on his head. Since the late 2000s people have told consistent stories of a silhouette of a man in a brimmed hat appearing between sleep and wakefulness; online he is often referenced as a hallucination brought on by diphenhydramine abuse.

claims.quote: the "Hat Man", who shares the characteristics of general shadow people but is named for a fedora or other brimmed hat on his head.

claims.quote: The foggy Santa Lucia Mountains run along the central coast of California, and for hundreds of years, the Chumash Indians and later residents have told of the Dark Watchers, shadowy hatted, caped figures who appear on ridges at twilight, only to fade away before your very eyes.

claims.quote: These explanations run the gamut, all the way from mistaken identification of a real shadow from an actual person or object, to various causes of optical illusions or hallucinations like drugs or hypnogogic sleeping states, even simply lying and making up the story.
