claims.quote: The Pugot ("decapitated one") is a mythical fiend that is found in the folklore of the Ilocos region of the Philippines. It can assume various shapes such as hogs, dogs or even as humans. However, it usually appears as a black, big headless being.

statement.id: Pugot ('yang terpenggal') adalah makhluk jahat mitos dalam cerita rakyat Ilocos, Filipina, yang dapat menjelma babi, anjing, atau manusia, tetapi biasanya tampak sebagai sosok besar hitam tanpa kepala.
statement.en: The pugot ('decapitated one') is a mythical fiend of Ilocos folklore in the Philippines that can become hogs, dogs or humans but usually appears as a big black headless being.

claims.quote: The creature usually resides in dark places or deserted houses. However, they especially like living in trees such as the duhat (Eugenia cumini), santol (Sandoricum koetjape), and tamarind.

statement.id: Pugot tinggal di tempat gelap atau rumah kosong, dan terutama suka tinggal di pohon seperti duwet, sentul, dan asam.
statement.en: The pugot lives in dark places or deserted houses, especially liking trees such as the duhat, santol and tamarind.

claims.quote: Aside from its shapeshifting abilities, the pugot can also move at great speeds, feeding on snakes and insects that it finds among the trees. It feeds by thrusting food through its neck stump. Although frightening, the pugot is otherwise relatively harmless.

statement.id: Selain dapat berubah wujud, pugot dapat bergerak sangat cepat dan memakan ular serta serangga di antara pepohonan dengan menyodorkan makanan ke tunggul lehernya; meski menakutkan, ia relatif tidak berbahaya.
statement.en: Besides shapeshifting, the pugot can move at great speed, feeding on snakes and insects among the trees by thrusting food through its neck stump; though frightening, it is relatively harmless.

claims.quote: The pugot is also found in the Ifugao myth "Tulud Nimputul: The Self-Beheaded" where he appears to the human hero. He was fed by the hero with chopped chicken meat that was mixed with blood.

statement.id: Pugot juga muncul dalam mitos Ifugao Tulud Nimputul: Si Pemenggal Diri, ketika sang pahlawan memberinya daging ayam cincang bercampur darah.
statement.en: The pugot appears in the Ifugao myth Tulud Nimputul: The Self-Beheaded, where the hero feeds it chopped chicken mixed with blood.

claims.quote: However, the creature is fond of women's underwear and takes them while they are being dried on a clothesline.

statement.id: Pugot gemar pakaian dalam perempuan dan mengambilnya saat dijemur di tali jemuran.
statement.en: The pugot is fond of women's underwear and takes it while it is being dried on a clothesline.

claims.quote: Suac and His Adventures. Narrated by Anastacia Villegas of Arayat, Pampanga, who heard the story from her grandmother.

statement.id: Kisah "Suac and His Adventures" dituturkan oleh Anastacia Villegas dari Arayat, Pampanga, yang mendengarnya dari neneknya.
statement.en: "Suac and His Adventures" was narrated by Anastacia Villegas of Arayat, Pampanga, who heard it from her grandmother.

claims.quote: saw on the top of the tree a horrible creature,—a very large black man with a long beard. This was Pugut.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Pampanga ini, pemburu melihat di puncak pohon makhluk mengerikan, seorang lelaki hitam sangat besar berjanggut panjang; itulah Pugut.
statement.en: In this Pampanga tale the hunter sees on top of a tree a horrible creature, a very large black man with a long beard; this was Pugut.

claims.quote: Pugut knocked the hunter down, and before he had time to recover had eaten up all the food.

statement.id: Pugut menjatuhkan si pemburu dan menghabiskan semua makanan sebelum ia sempat bangkit.
statement.en: Pugut knocks the hunter down and eats up all the food before he can recover.

claims.quote: But Suac placed the food near the fire and stood by it; and when Pugut tried to seize it, the boy pushed him into the fire. Pugut’s beard was burnt, and it became kinky.

statement.id: Suac menaruh makanan dekat api dan mendorong Pugut ke dalam api; janggut Pugut terbakar dan menjadi keriting.
statement.en: Suac places the food near the fire and pushes Pugut into it; Pugut's beard is burnt and becomes kinky.

claims.quote: Thus Pugut was destroyed. Suac then took his victim’s club, and returned under the tree.

statement.id: Suac mendorong Pugut ke mulut buaya sehingga Pugut binasa, lalu mengambil gada korbannya.
statement.en: Suac pushes Pugut into a crocodile's mouth, destroying him, and takes his victim's club.

claims.quote: After Suac has killed Pugut and has come into possession of his victim’s magic club, he easily slays a man-eating giant

statement.id: Catatan Fansler: setelah membunuh Pugut dan memperoleh gada sakti korbannya, Suac dengan mudah membunuh raksasa pemakan manusia.
statement.en: Fansler's notes: after killing Pugut and gaining his victim's magic club, Suac easily slays a man-eating giant.

claims.quote: We seem here to have a myth element explaining why the Negrito’s hair is kinky.

statement.id: Menurut catatan Fansler, tampaknya ada unsur mitos yang menjelaskan mengapa rambut orang Negrito keriting.
statement.en: Fansler's note suggests a myth element explaining why the Negrito's hair is kinky.

claims.quote: The root pugut is found in many of the dialects, and has two distinct meanings: (1) “a Negro or Negrito of the mountains;” (2) “decapitated, or with the hands or feet cut off.”

statement.id: Menurut Fansler, akar kata pugut ada di banyak dialek dengan dua arti: orang Negro atau Negrito pegunungan, dan "terpenggal" atau "terpotong tangan atau kakinya".
statement.en: According to Fansler, the root pugut is found in many dialects with two meanings: a Negro or Negrito of the mountains, and "decapitated, or with the hands or feet cut off".

claims.quote: Among the Tagalogs, Bicols, and Visayans, the word is not used to designate a night-appearing demon or monster.

statement.id: Fansler mencatat bahwa di antara orang Tagalog, Bicol, dan Visaya kata itu tidak dipakai untuk setan atau monster yang muncul malam hari.
statement.en: Fansler notes that among the Tagalogs, Bicols and Visayans the word is not used for a night-appearing demon or monster.

claims.quote: Tag. cafre, which is equivalent to Iloc. pugut, is Spanish for Kaffir.

statement.id: Fansler: cafre dalam bahasa Tagalog setara dengan pugut dalam bahasa Ilokano, dan berasal dari kata Spanyol untuk Kaffir.
statement.en: Fansler: Tagalog cafre is equivalent to Ilokano pugut and is Spanish for Kaffir.

claims.quote: Among the Ilocanos and Pampangos, the Pugot was a nocturnal spirit, usually in the form of a gigantic negro figure, terrifying, but not particularly harmful.

statement.id: Menurut The Aswang Project, di antara orang Ilocano dan Pampango, pugot adalah roh malam hari, biasanya berbentuk sosok negro raksasa, menakutkan tetapi tidak terlalu berbahaya.
statement.en: According to The Aswang Project, among the Ilocanos and Pampangos the pugot was a nocturnal spirit, usually a gigantic dark figure, terrifying but not particularly harmful.

claims.quote: It corresponded to the Tagalog Kapre, which eventually took ownership of the Pugot’s early attributes.

statement.id: Pugot setara dengan kapre dalam tradisi Tagalog, yang akhirnya mengambil alih ciri-ciri awal pugot.
statement.en: The pugot corresponded to the Tagalog kapre, which eventually took over the pugot's early attributes.

claims.quote: Its power of rapid transformation made it a more or less formidable opponent. Sometimes it took the form of a cat with fiery eyes, a minute later appearing as a large dog. Then it would turn into an enormous black negro smoking a large cigar, and finally disappear as a ball of fire.

statement.id: Kemampuannya berubah wujud dengan cepat membuatnya lawan yang tangguh: kadang berupa kucing bermata api, semenit kemudian anjing besar, lalu sosok hitam raksasa yang mengisap cerutu, dan akhirnya lenyap sebagai bola api.
statement.en: Its power of rapid transformation made it a formidable opponent: sometimes a cat with fiery eyes, a minute later a large dog, then an enormous black figure smoking a large cigar, finally disappearing as a ball of fire.

claims.quote: It lived either in large trees or in abandoned houses.

statement.id: Pugot tinggal di pohon besar atau rumah terbengkalai.
statement.en: The pugot lived either in large trees or in abandoned houses.

claims.quote: The earliest belief of the Pugot “spirit” is found in Ilocano myths as the spirits of ancestral aborigines (Aetas) who guard treasures.

statement.id: Menurut Jordan Clark, kepercayaan paling awal tentang "roh" pugot ada dalam mitos Ilocano sebagai roh penduduk asli leluhur (Aeta) yang menjaga harta karun.
statement.en: According to Jordan Clark, the earliest belief in the pugot "spirit" is found in Ilocano myths as the spirits of ancestral aborigines (Aetas) who guard treasures.

claims.quote: The term pugot denotes either “the black one,” “the decapitated one,” or “one with hands cut off,” and the creature is widely known by that name in Northern and Central Luzon
claims.locator: PUGOT: The Headless Being (quoting Maximo Ramos)

statement.id: The Aswang Project mengutip Maximo Ramos: pugot berarti "yang hitam", "yang terpenggal", atau "yang terpotong tangannya", dan makhluk ini dikenal dengan nama itu di Luzon utara dan tengah.
statement.en: The Aswang Project quotes Maximo Ramos: the term pugot denotes "the black one", "the decapitated one" or "one with hands cut off", and the creature is known by that name in Northern and Central Luzon.

claims.quote: Perhaps the Pugot was originally thought to be the spirits of the dishonoured and decapitated bodies that were not claimed by their relatives and given proper burial rites.

statement.id: Jordan Clark berspekulasi bahwa pugot mungkin semula dianggap roh jasad terhormat yang dipenggal dan tidak diklaim kerabat serta tidak diberi upacara pemakaman layak.
statement.en: Jordan Clark speculates that the pugot was perhaps originally thought to be the spirits of dishonoured, decapitated bodies not claimed by relatives and given proper burial rites.

claims.quote: Lastly, the killing of Catholic priests by the Ifugao in the late 19th century was incorporated into existing lowland superstition.

statement.id: Menurut Jordan Clark, pembunuhan pastor Katolik oleh orang Ifugao pada akhir abad ke-19 dimasukkan ke dalam takhayul dataran rendah yang sudah ada, sehingga muncul pugot sebagai pastor tanpa kepala.
statement.en: According to Jordan Clark, the killing of Catholic priests by the Ifugao in the late 19th century was incorporated into existing lowland superstition, giving rise to the pugot as a headless priest.

claims.quote: In the case of the Pugot, there are three clearly defined versions – and those don’t even touch on the horrific child eating version known as the Pugot Mamu!

statement.id: Jordan Clark menyebut ada tiga versi pugot yang jelas terdefinisi, belum termasuk versi pemakan anak yang dikenal sebagai Pugot Mamu.
statement.en: Jordan Clark says there are three clearly defined versions of the pugot, not counting the child-eating version known as the Pugot Mamu.

claims.quote: though less as a headless being than as “a black being that can assume varying sizes—from a man tiny as a new-born babe to a giant the size of a large acacia tree,”
claims.locator: PUGOT: The Headless Being (quoting Maximo Ramos)

statement.id: The Aswang Project mengutip Ramos: di Luzon utara dan tengah pugot lebih dikenal bukan sebagai makhluk tanpa kepala melainkan sebagai makhluk hitam yang ukurannya bisa berubah-ubah, dari sekecil bayi baru lahir hingga sebesar pohon akasia besar.
statement.en: The Aswang Project quotes Ramos: in Northern and Central Luzon the pugot is known less as a headless being than as a black being of varying size, from as tiny as a new-born babe to the size of a large acacia tree.

text.id: Dicatat dalam karya Li Dongyang dari zaman Dinasti Ming
text.en: Recorded in a work by Li Dongyang of the Ming Dynasty

short_description.id: Qiuniu adalah salah satu dari Sembilan Putra Naga menurut Li Dongyang, berwujud naga kecil kuning bersisik dan bertanduk. Ia menyukai musik dan wujudnya menghias alat musik berdawai.
short_description.en: Qiuniu is one of the Nine Sons of the Dragon according to Li Dongyang, a small yellow dragon with scales and horns. It loves music and its image decorates stringed instruments.

long_description.id: Qiuniu (囚牛, Shūgyū) adalah salah satu dari Sembilan Putra Naga menurut Li Dongyang dalam Huailutang ji. Wujudnya digambarkan sebagai naga kecil kuning yang bertanduk dan bersisik. Wikipedia bahasa Mandarin menyebutnya putra sulung dan mengutip Li Dongyang: seumur hidup ia gemar musik, dan binatang yang diukir di kepala huqin adalah wujud peninggalannya.
long_description.en: Qiuniu (囚牛, Shūgyū) is one of the Nine Sons of the Dragon according to Li Dongyang in the Huailutang ji. It is described as a small yellow dragon with horns and scales. Chinese Wikipedia calls it the eldest son and quotes Li Dongyang: it loved music all its life, and the beast carved on the head of the huqin is its remaining image.

long_description.id: Ia menyukai musik dan wujudnya menghias qin dan genderang. Wikipedia bahasa Mandarin menambahkan bahwa ia sangat mahir bermusik sehingga banyak kepala qin memakai wujudnya, dan wujudnya dengan kepala terangkat dan mulut terbuka terdapat pula pada huqin suku Han, yueqin berkepala naga suku Yi, sanxian suku Bai, dan sebagian alat musik suku Tibet.
long_description.en: It loves music and its image decorates qin and drums. Chinese Wikipedia adds that it was highly skilled in music so many qin heads use its likeness, and its raised-head, open-mouthed image is also found on the Han huqin, the Yi dragon-head yueqin, the Bai sanxian and some Tibetan instruments.

long_description.id: Beberapa teks Dinasti Ming memuat daftar Sembilan Putra Naga, dan daftar Li Dongyang (1447–1516) memuat sembilan makhluk. Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Inggris, sebagian makhluk dalam daftar itu berdasar pada makhluk yang lebih tua, tetapi kebanyakan tidak punya latar mitologis lain dan hanya dipakai sebagai nama struktur dekoratif.
long_description.en: Several Ming Dynasty texts give lists of the Nine Sons of the Dragon, and Li Dongyang's list (1447–1516) has nine creatures. English Wikipedia notes that a few creatures in the lists build on older beasts, while most lack any other mythological background and serve only as names for decorative structures.

cultural_context.id: Wujud Qiuniu dipakai sebagai hiasan kepala alat musik berdawai; secara umum, menurut Wikipedia bahasa Inggris, kebanyakan makhluk dalam daftar sembilan putra naga hanya dipakai sebagai nama struktur dekoratif.
cultural_context.en: Qiuniu's image is used as ornament on the heads of stringed instruments; more generally, according to English Wikipedia, most creatures in the nine-sons lists are merely used as names for decorative structures.

role.en: Fond of music; its image decorates stringed instruments and drums.

famous_for.en: Known as the music-loving dragon whose image is carved on instrument heads.

description.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Mandarin, ia sangat menyukai musik, gemar memainkan qin, dan sangat mahir dalam musik.
description.en: According to Chinese Wikipedia, it loved music, enjoyed playing the qin and was highly skilled in music.

note.id: Qiuniu adalah salah satu dari Sembilan Putra Naga menurut Li Dongyang.
note.en: Qiuniu is one of the Nine Sons of the Dragon according to Li Dongyang.

statement.id: Qiuniu adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga dalam kisah Li Dongyang.
statement.en: Qiuniu is one of the nine dragon sons in an account by Li Dongyang.

claims.quote: 囚牛（しゅうぎゅう）は、李東陽が著した『懐麓堂集』の説による竜生九子の一つ。姿は黄色い小さな龍の角と鱗を持つ。

statement.id: Gambarnya memiliki tanduk dan sisik naga kuning kecil.
statement.en: Its image includes a small yellow dragon’s horns and scales.

claims.quote: 音楽を好み、琴や鼓の飾りになっている。イー族の月琴、ペー族（白族：雲南省）の琴、他チベット系民族のいくつか楽器で見られる。

statement.id: Ia dikaitkan dengan musik dan menghiasi alat musik petik serta perkusi.
statement.en: It is associated with music and decorates string and percussion instruments.

claims.quote: 音楽を好み、琴や鼓の飾りになっている。イー族の月琴、ペー族（白族：雲南省）の琴、他チベット系民族のいくつか楽器で見られる。

statement.id: Contohnya terdapat pada alat musik masyarakat Yi, Bai, dan kelompok terkait Tibet.
statement.en: Examples occur on instruments of Yi, Bai and Tibetan-related peoples.

claims.quote: 囚牛，龍生九子中的長子，明朝李東陽所著《懷麓堂集》之〈記龍生九子〉篇中所記：「囚牛，龍種，平生好音樂，今胡琴頭上刻獸是其遺像。」

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Mandarin menyebut Qiuniu putra sulung dari Sembilan Putra Naga; ia mengutip Li Dongyang (Dinasti Ming) dalam Huailutang ji, bagian "Ji longsheng jiuzi": "Qiuniu, jenis naga, seumur hidup gemar musik; binatang yang kini diukir di kepala huqin adalah wujud peninggalannya."
statement.en: Chinese Wikipedia calls Qiuniu the eldest of the Nine Sons of the Dragon and quotes Li Dongyang of the Ming Dynasty in the Huailutang ji, section "Ji longsheng jiuzi": "Qiuniu, a dragon kind, loved music all his life; the beast carved on the head of the huqin today is his remaining image."

claims.quote: 形狀為有鱗角的黃色小龍，平生很喜歡音樂，酷愛彈琴，對音樂有很高的造詣，所以很多琴頭都用祂的造像。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Mandarin, bentuknya naga kecil kuning bersisik dan bertanduk; ia sangat menyukai musik dan gemar memainkan qin dengan keahlian tinggi, sehingga banyak kepala qin memakai wujudnya.
statement.en: According to Chinese Wikipedia, its shape is a small yellow dragon with scales and horns; it loved music and playing the qin and was highly skilled in music, so many qin heads use its likeness.

claims.quote: 例如：漢族的胡琴、彝族的龍頭月琴、白族的三弦琴以及藏族的一些樂器上也有其揚頭張口的形象。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Mandarin, wujudnya dengan kepala terangkat dan mulut terbuka juga terdapat pada huqin suku Han, yueqin berkepala naga suku Yi, sanxian suku Bai, dan sebagian alat musik suku Tibet.
statement.en: According to Chinese Wikipedia, its raised-head, open-mouthed image is also found on the Han huqin, the Yi dragon-head yueqin, the Bai sanxian and some Tibetan instruments.

claims.quote: There are four principal versions of the list: ... Li Dongyang's (李東陽 , 1447–1516) list, which includes 9 creatures

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Inggris menyebut daftar Li Dongyang (1447–1516), yang memuat 9 makhluk, sebagai salah satu dari empat versi utama daftar putra naga.
statement.en: English Wikipedia names Li Dongyang's (1447–1516) list, with 9 creatures, as one of four principal versions of the list of the dragon's children.

claims.quote: Several Ming Dynasty texts list what were claimed as the Nine Offspring of the Dragon (Chinese: 龍生九子), and subsequently these feature prominently in popular Chinese stories and writings.

statement.id: Beberapa teks Dinasti Ming memuat apa yang diklaim sebagai Sembilan Putra Naga, dan sejak itu menonjol dalam kisah dan tulisan populer Tiongkok.
statement.en: Several Ming Dynasty texts list what were claimed as the Nine Offspring of the Dragon, and subsequently these feature prominently in popular Chinese stories and writings.

short_description.id: Rhita Gawr adalah raksasa dalam cerita rakyat Welsh yang memakai mantel dari janggut raja-raja dan dibunuh Raja Arthur di Yr Wyddfa.
short_description.en: Rhita Gawr is a giant of Welsh folk tales who wore a cloak of kings' beards and was killed by King Arthur on Yr Wyddfa.

long_description.id: Rhita Gawr adalah tokoh cerita rakyat Welsh, raksasa yang konon memiliki mantel yang dibuat dari janggut raja-raja. Ia menuntut janggut Raja Arthur; Arthur menolak, dan keduanya bertarung di Yr Wyddfa. Rhita terbunuh dan dikuburkan prajurit Arthur di bawah tumpukan batu (carnedd) di puncak, yang menurut cerita memberi nama gunung itu: "gŵydd" (tumpukan batu) dengan "ma" (tempat) menjadi "Gwyddfa".
long_description.en: Rhita Gawr is a figure of Welsh folk tales, a giant said to own a cloak made from the beards of kings. He demanded King Arthur's beard; Arthur refused and they fought on Yr Wyddfa. Rhita was killed and Arthur's soldiers buried him under a cairn on the summit, which by the story named the mountain: 'gŵydd', cairn, joined to 'ma', place, giving 'Gwyddfa'.

long_description.id: Rhita juga dikaitkan dengan Meirionnydd dan didaftar dalam risalah tentang raksasa Wales karya Siôn Dafydd Rhys dari akhir abad ke-16; menurut satu versi ia tinggal di Yr Wyddfa dan dikubur di puncak Aran Benllyn dekat Llyn Tegid. Artikel ja menyamakannya dengan Ritho dalam Historia Regum Britanniae karya Geoffrey dari Monmouth, raksasa yang membuat mantel bulu dari janggut raja-raja yang dibunuhnya dan dikalahkan Arthur.
long_description.en: Rhita is also tied to Meirionnydd and is listed in Siôn Dafydd Rhys's late 16th-century essay on the giants of Wales; one version has him living on Yr Wyddfa and buried on top of Aran Benllyn near Llyn Tegid. The ja article identifies him with Ritho of Geoffrey of Monmouth's Historia Regum Britanniae, a giant who made a fur cloak from the beards of the kings he slew and was overcome by Arthur.

long_description.id: Dalam teks Geoffrey of Monmouth, Arthur menyatakan telah membunuh raksasa Ritho di gunung Aravius. Raksasa itu membuat bulu dari janggut raja-raja yang dibunuhnya, mengirim pesan agar Arthur mengirimkan janggutnya, dan menantangnya berduel jika menolak, dengan taruhan bulu itu dan janggut yang kalah. Arthur menang dan mengambil janggut serta rampasan sang raksasa.
long_description.en: In the text of Geoffrey of Monmouth, Arthur says he killed the giant Ritho on the mountain Aravius. The giant made furs from the beards of kings he had killed, sent word that Arthur should send him his beard, and challenged him to a duel if he refused, with the furs and the loser's beard as the stakes. Arthur won and took the giant's beard and spoils.

short_description.id: Seelkee adalah monster danau berkepala kuda dari rawa Chilliwack, British Columbia, yang konon dilihat orang Stó:lō selama ratusan tahun [seelkee-c01, seelkee-c02, seelkee-c03].
short_description.en: Seelkee is a horse-headed lake monster of the Chilliwack swamps, British Columbia, reportedly seen by the Stó:lō for centuries [seelkee-c01, seelkee-c02, seelkee-c03].

long_description.id: Seelkee adalah monster danau yang konon hidup di rawa-rawa Chilliwack, British Columbia [seelkee-c01], dan telah dilihat orang Stó:lō selama ratusan tahun [seelkee-c02]. Ia paling sering digambarkan seperti ular laut berkepala kuda sepanjang 10 hingga 15 kaki [seelkee-c03], atau ular berkepala dua berwarna hitam berpola merah [seelkee-c04]. Motifnya menghiasi tiang rumah panjang Stó:lō [seelkee-c05].
long_description.en: Seelkee is a lake monster said to live in the swamps of Chilliwack, British Columbia [seelkee-c01], seen by the Stó:lō for centuries [seelkee-c02]. It is most often a horse-headed, sea-serpent-like beast 10 to 15 feet long [seelkee-c03], or a two-headed black snake with red designs [seelkee-c04]. Its image decorated Stó:lō longhouse posts [seelkee-c05].

long_description.id: Dalam tulisan Museum Chilliwack, makhluk ini disebut s’í:lhqey, yang hidup di saluran berkelok dan rawa dan biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular berkepala dua [seelkee-c06]. Menurut tulisan itu, s’í:lhqey berkuasa membuat tubuh orang terpelintir dan sakit sampai mati jika orang itu lari ketika melihatnya [seelkee-c07].
long_description.en: In a Chilliwack Museum piece, the creature is called s’í:lhqey, living in winding channels and marshlands and normally described as a serpent with two heads [seelkee-c06]. According to the piece, s’í:lhqey have the power to twist a person's body and make them sick until death if the person runs on seeing the creature [seelkee-c07].

long_description.id: Keterangan gambar di halaman museum, yang diambil dari buku Oliver N. Wells terbitan 1970 [seelkee-c12], memuat kesaksian lisan: ular besar berkepala kuda yang panjang dan halus, bermulut panjang dan bertelinga panjang seperti kuda [seelkee-c08]. Kesaksian lain mengatakan makhluk itu bisa terbang dari danau ke danau [seelkee-c09], dan penuturnya menyebutnya SEEL-kee [seelkee-c13]. Dalam satu kisah, seorang pria membunuhnya dengan memasukkan rumput ke mulutnya [seelkee-c10] lalu melukis ular itu di atas pintu rumah besarnya untuk melindungi rumah tersebut [seelkee-c11].
long_description.en: The image captions on the museum page, taken from Oliver N. Wells's book published in 1970 [seelkee-c12], record oral accounts: a big snake with a long, smooth horse's head, a long mouth and long horse-like ears [seelkee-c08]. Another account says it could fly from lake to lake [seelkee-c09], and its speaker calls it a SEEL-kee [seelkee-c13]. In one account a man killed it by throwing grass into its mouth [seelkee-c10] and then painted the serpent over the door of his big house to protect the house [seelkee-c11].

cultural_context.id: Motif Seelkee bercat merah menghiasi tiang rumah panjang di desa Stó:lō [seelkee-c05]. Dalam kisah yang dikutip museum, gambar ular di atas pintu dilukis untuk melindungi rumah [seelkee-c11].
cultural_context.en: Red-painted Seelkee designs decorated Stó:lō longhouse posts [seelkee-c05]. In an account quoted by the museum, the serpent's image over the door was painted to protect the house [seelkee-c11].

claims.quote: In Canadian folklore, Seelkee (transcribed in English from Halqemeylem, the local indigenous language) is a lake monster reported to have lived in the swamps of what is now Chilliwack, in British Columbia, Canada.

short_description.id: Shenlong adalah naga roh dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang menguasai hujan dan badai.
short_description.en: Shenlong is a Chinese mythological spirit dragon governing rain and tempests.

long_description.id: Shenlong adalah naga roh dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang menguasai hujan dan badai. Shenlong disebut dewa badai dan penguasa hujan.
long_description.en: Shenlong is a Chinese mythological spirit dragon governing rain and tempests. Shenlong is described as a god of tempest and master of rain.

long_description.id: Naga roh ini digambarkan bersisik biru langit dan menguasai badai, awan, dan hujan yang menjadi sandaran kehidupan pertanian. Teks klasik Guanzi menjelaskan bahwa naga lahir di air dan mengembara dengan lima warna sehingga disebut ilahi; ia dapat mengecil menjadi seperti ulat sutra, membesar hingga bersembunyi di bawah langit, naik melampaui awan, atau turun ke mata air dalam.
long_description.en: This spirit dragon is described as azure-scaled and governing the storms, clouds and rain on which agricultural life depends. The classical text Guanzi explains that the dragon is born in water and roams in five colors, hence it is called divine; it can shrink to a silkworm, grow so large it hides beneath heaven, rise above the clouds or descend into deep springs.

long_description.id: Naskah klasik lain menggambarkan naga secara umum dengan cara serupa. Kamus Shuowen Jiezi menyebut naga yang tertua di antara makhluk bersisik, dapat tersembunyi atau terang, kecil atau besar, naik ke langit pada ekuinoks musim semi. Bencao Gangmu menyebut napas naga membentuk awan dan ia dapat berubah menjadi air atau api, dan mencatat bahwa naga takut pada besi, rumput wangcao, kelabang, daun chinaberry, dan benang lima warna.
long_description.en: Other classical works describe the dragon in general in similar terms. The Shuowen Jiezi dictionary calls the dragon the chief of scaly creatures, able to be hidden or bright, small or huge, rising to heaven at the spring equinox. The Bencao Gangmu says the dragon's breath forms clouds and it can change into water or fire, and records that it fears iron, wangcao grass, centipedes, chinaberry leaves and five-colored silk.

claims.quote: Shenlong (simplified Chinese: 神龙; traditional Chinese: 神龍; pinyin: shén lóng, literally "god dragon" or "divine dragon", Japanese: 神龍, shinryū) is the spirit dragon from Chinese mythology who is the dragon god of the tempest and also a master of rain.

statement.id: Shenlong adalah naga roh dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang menguasai hujan dan badai.
statement.en: Shenlong is a Chinese mythological spirit dragon governing rain and tempests.

claims.quote: is the spirit dragon from Chinese mythology who is the dragon god of the tempest and also a master of rain.

statement.id: Shenlong disebut dewa badai dan penguasa hujan.
statement.en: Shenlong is described as a god of tempest and master of rain.

claims.quote: 龍生於水，被五色而游，故神。欲小則化如蠶蠋，欲大則藏於天下，欲上則凌於雲氣，欲下則入於深泉。變化無日，上下無時，謂之神。

statement.id: Teks klasik Guanzi ini menyatakan naga (龍) lahir di air dan mengembara dengan lima warna sehingga disebut "shen" (ilahi); ia dapat mengecil menjadi seperti ulat sutra, membesar hingga bersembunyi di bawah langit, naik melampaui awan, atau turun ke mata air dalam, dan perubahannya tak terikat hari maupun waktu.
statement.en: This classical text, the Guanzi, states that the dragon (龍) is born in water and roams wearing five colors, hence it is "shen" (divine); it can shrink to a silkworm, grow so large it hides beneath heaven, rise above the clouds or descend into deep springs, and its changes are not bound to day or time.

claims.quote: The spiritual dragon is azure-scaled and governs the storms, clouds, and rain on which all agricultural life depends.

statement.id: Naga roh ini bersisik biru langit dan menguasai badai, awan, dan hujan yang menjadi sandaran seluruh kehidupan pertanian.
statement.en: The spiritual dragon is azure-scaled and governs the storms, clouds and rain on which all agricultural life depends.

claims.quote: 龍（ ）：鱗蟲之長。能幽，能明，能細，能巨，能短，能長；春分而登天，秋分而潛淵。

statement.id: Dalam teks kamus klasik Shuowen Jiezi, naga (龍) adalah yang tertua di antara makhluk bersisik; ia dapat tersembunyi atau terang, kecil atau besar, pendek atau panjang, naik ke langit pada ekuinoks musim semi dan menyelam ke samudra pada ekuinoks musim gugur.
statement.en: In the classical dictionary text Shuowen Jiezi, the dragon (龍) is the chief of scaly creatures; it can be hidden or bright, small or huge, short or long, rising to heaven at the spring equinox and diving into the deep at the autumn equinox.

claims.quote: 頭上有博山，又名尺木，龍無尺木不能升天。呵氣成雲，既能變水，又能變火。

statement.id: Bencao Gangmu karya Li Shizhen menyebut naga memiliki "Boshan" atau "chimu" di kepalanya, yang tanpanya naga tidak dapat naik ke langit, dan bahwa napasnya membentuk awan serta dapat mengubah diri menjadi air atau api.
statement.en: Li Shizhen's Bencao Gangmu says the dragon has a "Boshan", also called "chimu", on its head, without which it cannot ascend to heaven, and that its breath forms clouds and it can change into water or fire.

claims.quote: 龍性粗猛，而愛美玉、空青，喜嗜燕肉，畏鐵及菵草、蜈蚣、楝葉、五色絲。

statement.id: Menurut Bencao Gangmu, naga bersifat kasar dan garang, menyukai batu giok indah dan kongqing serta daging burung layang-layang, dan takut pada besi, rumput wangcao, kelabang, daun chinaberry, dan benang lima warna.
statement.en: According to the Bencao Gangmu, the dragon's nature is rough and fierce; it loves fine jade and kongqing and is fond of swallow meat, and fears iron, wangcao grass, centipedes, chinaberry leaves and five-colored silk.

short_description.id: Shippeitarō adalah anjing penolong dalam dongeng Jepang berjudul sama. Ia dititipkan sebagai pengganti gadis korban dan mengalahkan roh jahat bersama seorang pemuda pejuang.
short_description.en: Shippeitarō is a helper dog in the Japanese fairy tale of the same name. Put in a sacrificial maiden's place, he helps a young warrior vanquish evil spirits.

long_description.id: Shippeitarō (しっぺい太郎 atau 竹篦太郎; ejaan Schippeitaro) adalah nama anjing penolong dalam dongeng Jepang berjudul sama. Seorang pemuda pejuang mendengar para roh membisikkan bahwa yang dapat mencelakakan mereka adalah "Shippeitaro", yang ternyata seekor anjing.
long_description.en: Shippeitarō (しっぺい太郎 or 竹篦太郎; "Schippeitaro" in the German spelling) is a dog that helps the hero of a Japanese fairy tale bearing the same title. A young warrior overhears spirits hinting that what could bring them down is "Shippeitaro", which proves to be a dog.

long_description.id: Anjing itu ditaruh dalam peti pengorbanan sebagai ganti gadis, dan ketika roh-roh datang, pemuda dan anjing menyerang kucing-kucing itu dan mengalahkan mereka. Dalam The Violet Fairy Book, penduduk menjawab bahwa Schippeitaro adalah anjing milik pengawas pangeran; para kucing menari di kapel hutan, dan Roh Gunung berupa kucing hitam raksasa yang digigit anjing itu lalu dipenggal pemuda.
long_description.en: The dog is placed in the sacrificial container in place of the maiden, and when the spirits arrive, the warrior and dog attack and vanquish the cats. In the Violet Fairy Book, the villagers say Schippeitaro is the dog of their prince's overseer; the cats dance in a forest chapel, and the Spirit of the Mountain is a huge black cat that the dog bites and the youth beheads.

long_description.id: Roh jahat tampil sebagai monyet dalam sebagian besar versi, seperti dalam antologi Keigo Seki, tetapi sebagai kucing dalam versi James dan The Violet Fairy Book. Para folklorist menggolongkan kisah ini ke tipe "Destroying the Monkey Demon" (Sarugami taiji). Di akhir versi The Violet Fairy Book, gadis gunung selamat dan pesta tahunan diadakan untuk mengenang pemuda dan anjingnya.
long_description.en: The evil spirits appear as monkeys in most versions, as in Keigo Seki's anthology, but as cats in James's version and the Violet Fairy Book. Folklorists class the tale under the "Destroying the Monkey Demon" (Sarugami taiji) type. At the end of the Violet Fairy Book version the mountain girls are safe and a yearly feast is held in memory of the youth and his dog.

short_description.id: Siuru adalah burung dongeng dalam lagu rakyat Estonia lama dan epos Kalevipoeg, "putri Taara" yang sayapnya lebih ringan dari angin.
short_description.en: Siuru is a fabulous bird of old Estonian folk songs and the Kalevipoeg epic, "daughter of Taara" with wings lighter than the wind.

long_description.id: Siuru atau Siurulind adalah burung dongeng dalam lagu-lagu rakyat Estonia lama, yang juga disebut dalam nyanyian kesembilan belas epos Kalevipoeg. Namanya dikaitkan dengan kata Finlandia kiuru, "burung lark".
long_description.en: Siuru or Siurulind is a fabulous bird of old Estonian folk songs, also mentioned in the nineteenth canto of the Kalevipoeg epic. Its name is linked with the Finnish word kiuru, "lark".

long_description.id: Dalam Kalevipoeg, Siuru disebut putri Taara, burung bersayap biru yang menetas tanpa ibu dan tumbuh tanpa saudara; Uku tua memberinya sayap lebih ringan dari angin agar bisa terbang. Orang Estonia lama memperdebatkan apakah Siuru manusia atau burung; yang menganggapnya manusia merujuk pada sebutan Kreutzwald, "putri Taara".
long_description.en: In the Kalevipoeg, Siuru is called the daughter of Taara, a blue-winged bird hatched without a mother and raised without siblings; old Uku gave her wings lighter than the wind so she could fly. Estonians have long debated whether Siuru is a person or a bird; those who say a person point to Kreutzwald's phrase "daughter of Taara".

long_description.id: Eisen, dalam karyanya tentang kepercayaan lama, menyatakan bahwa Siuru berasal dari Kreutzwald, seperti Vanemuine dan Ilmarine berasal dari Fählmann, dan bahwa semua yang berkaitan dengan Siuru ditambahkan Kreutzwald, meski bahan dasarnya ada dalam lagu rakyat. Menurut Eisen, Siuru tidak punya sarang dan Uku datang menolongnya dengan membuatkan sayap agar ia dapat terbang jauh; ia juga berpendapat bahwa "putri Taara" hanyalah nama kiasan dan Siuru tetap anggota keluarga burung. Dalam teks nyanyian kesembilan belas Kalevipoeg, si kakek menyiapkan sayap angin bagi sang putri, dan ia terbang jauh melintasi tiga dunia.
long_description.en: Eisen, in his work on old beliefs, states that Siuru was received from Kreutzwald, as Vanemuine and Ilmarine were from Fählmann, and that everything connected with Siuru was added by Kreutzwald, although the underlying material exists in folk song. According to Eisen, Siuru had no nest and Uku came to her aid by making wings so that she could fly far; he also holds that "Taara's daughter" is only a figurative name and that Siuru remains a member of the bird family. In the text of canto XIX of the Kalevipoeg, the grandfather prepares wind-wings for the daughter, and she flies far over three worlds.

short_description.id: Strix adalah burung pembawa sial dalam mitologi Klasik yang memakan daging dan darah manusia; dalam Fasti Ovidius ia menyerang bayi pada malam hari.
short_description.en: The strix is an ill-omened bird of classical mythology that fed on human flesh and blood; in Ovidius' Fasti it attacks infants by night.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Klasik, strix adalah burung pembawa sial hasil perubahan wujud yang memakan daging dan darah manusia. Istilah ini juga dipakai untuk penyihir dan makhluk jahat serupa.
long_description.en: In classical mythology the strix was an ill-omened bird of metamorphosis feeding on human flesh and blood. The term also referred to witches and similar malevolent beings.

long_description.id: Dalam Fasti karya Ovidius, strix digambarkan berkepala besar, bermata melotot, berparuh untuk merampas, berbulu kelabu berbercak, dan bercakar berkait. Mereka terbang pada malam hari, menyerang anak-anak tanpa pengasuh, dan dikatakan mencabik daging bayi susuan dengan paruh mereka. Namanya, menurut Ovidius, berasal dari kebiasaan mereka memekik mengerikan pada malam hari.
long_description.en: In Ovid's Fasti the strix is described with a big head, goggle eyes, a beak formed for rapine, feathers blotched with grey and hooked claws. They fly by night, attack nurseless children, and are said to rend the flesh of sucklings with their beaks. Their name, according to Ovid, comes from their habit of screeching horribly by night.

long_description.id: Ovidius menyatakan bahwa entah mereka lahir sebagai burung atau nenek-nenek yang diubah oleh mantra, mereka datang ke kamar Proca dan menyedot bayi berusia lima hari; sebatang tongkat Janus dari semak duri putih diletakkan di tempat jendela kecil menerangi kamar, dan sesudahnya burung-burung itu tidak lagi mengganggu buaian. Plinius menganggap cerita tentang burung hantu pekik yang menyemprotkan susu ke bibir bayi sebagai dongeng, dan mencatat bahwa nama strix dipakai dalam kutukan, tetapi burung apa yang dimaksud tidak jelas.
long_description.en: Ovid states that whether they are born birds or beldames transformed by a spell, they came into the chambers of Proca and sucked an infant five days old; a rod of Janus from the white-thorn was placed where a small window lit the chambers, and afterwards the birds did not violate the cradle. Pliny regards the stories of the screech-owl ejecting milk upon infants' lips as fabulous, and records that the name strix was used in maledictions, though what bird is meant is not well ascertained.

short_description.id: Teng atau Tengshe adalah naga terbang dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Teng, or Tengshe, is a flying dragon of Chinese mythology.

long_description.id: Teng atau Tengshe adalah naga terbang dalam mitologi Tiongkok. Sebutan Tengshe dapat bermakna ular naga terbang atau ular yang melayang. Dari makna aslinya, tengshe juga memperoleh makna sebagai rasi bintang, formasi tempur, dan garis fisiognomi di atas mulut.
long_description.en: Teng, or Tengshe, is a flying dragon of Chinese mythology. Tengshe may denote a flying-dragon snake or soaring snake. From its original meaning, tengshe also came to mean an asterism, a battle formation, and a physiognomic line above the mouth.

long_description.id: Aksara teng menggabungkan unsur fonetik dengan unsur serangga. Komentar Guo Pu atas Erya menggambarkannya melayang dalam awan dan kabut. Bencao Gangmu menyebut ular terbang tanpa kaki ini berubah menjadi naga dan dapat menunggangi awan, sementara teks klasik mengatakan ia mengembara di kabut tetapi menjadi sama dengan cacing dan semut ketika awan bubar.
long_description.en: The teng character combines a phonetic component with an insect component. Guo Pu's Erya commentary describes it drifting through clouds and mist. The Bencao Gangmu says this footless flying snake turns into a dragon and can ride the clouds, while a classical text says it wanders in the mist but becomes no better than earthworms and ants when the clouds disperse.

long_description.id: Huainanzi menyebut ular yang naik dapat melayang di kabut tetapi terancam oleh kelabang. Xunzi, seorang Konfusianis, mencatat idiom bahwa ular itu terbang tanpa kaki, yang secara kiasan berarti keberhasilan datang dari memusatkan diri pada kemampuan sendiri.
long_description.en: The Huainanzi says the ascending snake can drift in the mist but is endangered by the centipede. Xunzi, a Confucianist, records the idiom that the snake flies without feet, which figuratively means success comes from concentrating on one's abilities.

cultural_context.id: Idiom tengshe wuzu er fei secara kiasan berarti bahwa keberhasilan datang dari memusatkan diri pada kemampuan sendiri.
cultural_context.en: The idiom tengshe wuzu er fei figuratively means that success comes from concentrating on one's own abilities.

claims.quote: Teng (Chinese: 螣; pinyin: téng; Wade–Giles: tʻêng) or Tengshe (traditional Chinese: 螣蛇／騰蛇; simplified Chinese: 螣蛇／腾蛇; pinyin: téngshé; Wade–Giles: tʻêng-shê; lit. 'soaring snake') is a flying dragon in Chinese mythology.

statement.id: Teng atau Tengshe adalah naga terbang dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
statement.en: Teng, or Tengshe, is a flying dragon of Chinese mythology.

claims.quote: This legendary creature's names include teng (螣; "a flying dragon") and tengshe (螣蛇; "flying-dragon snake" or 騰蛇; "soaring snake").

statement.id: Sebutan Tengshe dapat bermakna ular naga terbang atau ular yang melayang.
statement.en: Tengshe may denote a flying-dragon snake or soaring snake.

claims.quote: The Chinese character 螣 for teng graphically combines a phonetic element of zhen (朕) with the "insect radical" 虫. This radical is typically used in characters for insects, worms, reptiles, and dragons, such as in shen (蜃; "a sea-monster dragon") or jiao (蛟; "an aquatic dragon").

statement.id: Aksara teng menggabungkan unsur fonetik dengan unsur serangga.
statement.en: The teng character combines a phonetic component with an insect component.

claims.quote: The (3rd–2nd centuries BCE) Erya dictionary (16) defines teng (螣) as tengshe (螣蛇; "teng-snake"), and Guo Pu's commentary glosses it as a "[飛龍; feilong] flying dragon that drifts in the clouds and mist".

statement.id: Komentar Guo Pu atas Erya menggambarkannya melayang dalam awan dan kabut.
statement.en: Guo Pu's Erya commentary describes it drifting through clouds and mist.

claims.quote: From the original "flying dragon; flying serpent" denotation, tengshe acquired three additional meanings: "an asterism" in Traditional Chinese star names, "a battle formation" in Chinese military history, and "lines above the mouth" in physiognomy.

statement.id: Dari makna asli "naga terbang; ular terbang", tengshe memperoleh tiga makna tambahan: "rasi bintang" dalam nama bintang tradisional Tiongkok, "formasi tempur" dalam sejarah militer Tiongkok, dan "garis di atas mulut" dalam ilmu fisiognomi.
statement.en: From the original "flying dragon; flying serpent" meaning, tengshe acquired three further meanings: "an asterism" in traditional Chinese star names, "a battle formation" in Chinese military history, and "lines above the mouth" in physiognomy.

claims.quote: Confucianist Xunzi ... first records the Classical Chinese idiom tengshe wuzu er fei ... "flying dragon is without feet yet flies", which figuratively means "success results from concentrating on one's abilities".

statement.id: Xunzi, seorang Konfusianis, pertama kali mencatat idiom Tionghoa klasik tengshe wuzu er fei, "naga terbang tidak berkaki namun terbang", yang secara kiasan berarti "keberhasilan datang dari memusatkan diri pada kemampuan sendiri".
statement.en: The Confucianist Xunzi first records the Classical Chinese idiom tengshe wuzu er fei, "flying dragon is without feet yet flies", which figuratively means "success results from concentrating on one's abilities".

claims.quote: Huainanzi uses both tengshe graphic variants ... The ascending snake can drift in the mist, yet it is endangered by the centipede.

statement.id: Dalam Huainanzi, ular yang naik (tengshe) dapat melayang di dalam kabut, namun terancam oleh kelabang.
statement.en: In the Huainanzi, the ascending snake (tengshe) can drift in the mist yet is endangered by the centipede.

claims.quote: The (1578 CE) Bencao Gangmu ... "There are flying snakes without feet such as the 螣蛇 (T'eng She)." ... The t'eng-she changes into a dragon. This divine snake can ride upon the clouds and fly about over a thousand miles.

statement.id: Dalam Bencao Gangmu (1578), ular terbang tanpa kaki seperti 螣蛇 (T'eng She) disebut; komentarnya menyatakan bahwa t'eng-she berubah menjadi naga, ular ilahi ini dapat menunggangi awan dan terbang lebih dari seribu mil.
statement.en: The Bencao Gangmu (1578) mentions flying snakes without feet such as the 螣蛇 (T'eng She); its commentary says the t'eng-she changes into a dragon, and this divine snake can ride the clouds and fly over a thousand miles.

claims.quote: 慎子曰：飛龍乘雲，騰蛇遊霧，雲罷霧霽，而龍蛇與螾螘同矣，則失其所乘也。

statement.id: Shenzi (慎子) berkata bahwa naga terbang (飛龍) menunggangi awan dan ular terbang (騰蛇) mengembara di kabut, tetapi ketika awan bubar dan kabut cerah, naga dan ular itu sama saja dengan cacing dan semut karena kehilangan apa yang ditungganginya.
statement.en: Shenzi (慎子) says the flying dragon (飛龍) rides the clouds and the rising snake (騰蛇) wanders in the mist, but when clouds disperse and mist clears, the dragon and snake become the same as earthworms and ants because they lose what they ride.

short_description.id: Thunderdell adalah raksasa berkepala dua dari Cornwall dalam kisah Jack the Giant-Killer; ia datang untuk membalas dendam atas sanak-saudaranya, tetapi dikalahkan Jack.
short_description.en: Thunderdell is a two-headed giant of Cornwall in the tale of Jack the Giant-Killer; he comes to avenge his kinsmen but is defeated by Jack.

long_description.id: Thunderdell (Welsh: Taranau) adalah raksasa berkepala dua dari Cornwall yang dibunuh Jack the Giant-Killer dalam kisah-kisah yang dicatat Tabart dan lainnya. Namanya juga tercatat sebagai Thunderdel, Thunderel, Thundrel, Thunderdale, atau Thunderbore.
long_description.en: Thunderdell (Welsh: Taranau) is a Cornish giant with two heads who falls to Jack the Giant-Killer in tales such as those told by Tabart. The name is also recorded as Thunderdel, Thunderel, Thundrel, Thunderdale, or Thunderbore.

long_description.id: Dalam salah satu penceritaan, Thunderdell, raksasa berkepala dua, telah mendengar kematian sanak-saudaranya dan datang dari lembah-lembah utara (northern dales) untuk membalas dendam kepada Jack. Ia mencium kedatangan Jack yang tak terlihat, menyerukan "Fee, fi, fo, fum!", dan mengancam akan mencabik dan menggiling tulang Jack.
long_description.en: In one telling, news of his kinsmen's deaths reaches Thunderdell, a two-headed giant, who travels from the northern dales to take revenge on Jack. He smells the unseen Jack's approach, cries "Fee, fi, fo, fum!", and threatens to tear him apart and grind his bones.

long_description.id: Jack mengalahkan raksasa itu dengan tipu daya yang memakai parit dan jembatan angkat: berat si raksasa mematahkan jembatan sehingga ia tercebur ke air. Jack lalu menariknya ke tepi dengan tali dan kuda, memenggal kedua kepalanya, dan mengirimkannya kepada Raja Arthur. Versi tahun 1800 menyebutnya "Thunderful" dari Kutub Utara.
long_description.en: Jack defeats the giant with a trick involving the moat and drawbridge: the giant's weight breaks the bridge and he tumbles into the water. Jack then draws him ashore with a rope and horses, cuts off both heads, and sends them to King Arthur. A version from 1800 calls him "Thunderful", from the North Pole.

statement.id: Thunderdell (Welsh: Taranau; Thunderdel, Thunderel, Thundrel, Thunderdale, Thunderbore), raksasa berkepala dua Cornwall dibunuh Jack the Giant-Killer (Jack the Giant Killer) dalam kisah Tabart.
statement.en: Thunderdell (Welsh: Taranau; Thunderdel, Thunderel, Thundrel, Thunderdale, Thunderbore), a two-headed Cornish giant slain by Jack the Giant-Killer in Tabart's stories.

claims.quote: In Jack the Giant Killer, Thunderdell first appeared where he crashed a banquet that was prepared for Jack. During this time, he chanted "fee fau fum." Jack defeats and beheads the two-headed giant with a trick involving the house's moat and drawbridge.

statement.en: In Jack the Giant Killer, Thunderdell first appears crashing a banquet prepared for Jack, chanting "fee fau fum"; Jack defeats and beheads the two-headed giant with a trick involving the house's moat and drawbridge.

claims.quote: According to one version of the story from 1800, Thunderdell (here identified as "Thunderful") hails from the North Pole. statement.en: According to one version of the story from 1800, Thunderdell (here called "Thunderful") hails from the North Pole; he attacks Jack's banquet to avenge the deaths of two giants he had earlier slain, but is defeated and his heads are sent to King Arthur's court.

short_description.id: Tiangou adalah makhluk legenda Tiongkok berupa anjing hitam atau meteor.
short_description.en: Tiangou is a Chinese legendary creature resembling a black dog or meteor.

long_description.id: Tiangou adalah makhluk legenda Tiongkok berupa anjing hitam atau meteor. Makhluk ini dipercaya memakan matahari atau bulan saat gerhana.
long_description.en: Tiangou is a Chinese legendary creature resembling a black dog or meteor. This creature is believed to eat the sun or moon during an eclipse.

long_description.id: Dalam varian baik, ia menyerupai rubah berkepala putih yang memberikan perlindungan. Varian buruk menggambarkannya sebagai anjing hitam pemakan bulan. Sebuah kisah menyebut Ibu Suri dari Barat menangkap anjing dan menjadikannya penjaga gerbang langit. Zhang Xian digambarkan sebagai lawannya yang menggunakan busur dan panah.
long_description.en: In a benevolent variant, it resembles a white-headed fox offering protection. The adverse variant portrays it as a black dog that eats the moon. One tale describes the Queen Mother of the West capturing the dog and making it heaven's gatekeeper. Zhang Xian is portrayed as its adversary using a bow and arrows.

long_description.id: Dalam Shanhaijing, Tiangou di Gunung Yin berbentuk seperti 狸 berkepala putih, bersuara seperti "liuliu", dan dapat dipakai untuk menangkal bencana. Dalam Shiji, 天狗 adalah tanda langit berbentuk seperti bintang jatuh besar yang bagian bawahnya menyerupai anjing saat jatuh ke bumi, dan mengisyaratkan pasukan hancur serta jenderal terbunuh.
long_description.en: In the Shanhaijing, the Tiangou on Mount Yin is shaped like a white-headed 狸, cries like "liuliu" and can be used to ward off calamity. In the Shiji, the 天狗 is a heavenly sign shaped like a great shooting star whose lower part resembles a dog as it falls to earth, portending armies broken and generals killed.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda gerhana bulan, anjing hitam milik Hou Yi menjilat sisa pil keabadian, membesar, dan memakan Bulan bersama Chang'e; ia lalu memuntahkannya kembali. Zhang Xian, dewa kelahiran dan pelindung anak laki-laki, digambarkan sebagai musuhnya yang membidikkan busur dan panah ke langit.
long_description.en: In the lunar-eclipse legend, Hou Yi's black dog licked the remains of the immortality pill, grew large and ate the Moon along with Chang'e; it then spat them back out. Zhang Xian, the god of birth and protector of male children, is shown as its enemy aiming a bow and arrows at the sky.

description.id: Menurut Shanhaijing, Tiangou dapat dipakai untuk menangkal bencana; dalam varian baik, ia memberi perlindungan dari berbagai kesulitan dan perampok.
description.en: According to the Shanhaijing, the Tiangou can be used to ward off calamity; in its benevolent variant it gives protection from all sorts of troubles and robbers.

description.id: Zhang Xian, musuh tiangou, dikatakan melindungi anak-anaknya dari dewa anjing itu dengan busur dan panah.
description.en: Zhang Xian, the enemy of the tiangou, is said to protect his children from the dog god with his bow and arrows.

It is referred to by astrologers as a constellation guardian of welfare. This asterism consists of seven stars. In ancient Chinese astronomy, Tiangou ('Heavenly Dog') referred to an asterism located in the region of Argo Navis.

According to the legends, as an interpretation of a lunar eclipse, after Houyi shot down the nine Suns in the sky, he was awarded with an immortality-granting pill by the Queen Mother of the West. Before he could eat it, his wife Chang'e consumed the elixir of immortality. Chang'e felt her body getting lighter and flew away.

claims.quote: 曰陰山。濁浴之水出焉，而南流注于蕃澤，其中多文貝〈餘泉蚳之𩔖也，見爾雅。〉。有獸焉，其狀如狸〈或作豹。〉而白首，名曰天狗，其音如榴榴〈或作猫猫。〉，可以禦凶。

statement.id: Teks klasik Shanhaijing ini menyebut di Gunung Yin ada binatang berbentuk seperti 狸 (binatang kecil mirip kucing liar) berkepala putih, bernama Tiangou ("anjing langit"), bersuara seperti "liuliu", dan dapat dipakai untuk menangkal bencana.
statement.en: This classical text, the Shanhaijing, says that on Mount Yin there is a beast shaped like a 狸 (a wildcat-like small animal) with a white head, named Tiangou ("heavenly dog"), whose cry sounds like "liuliu", and which can be used to ward off calamity.

claims.quote: 天狗，狀如大奔星，〈【集解】孟康曰：「星有尾，旁有短彗，下有如狗形者，亦太白之精。」〉有聲，其下止地，類狗。所墮及，望之如火光炎炎〈【索隱】艷音也。〉衝天。其下圜如數頃田處，上兌者則有黃色，千里破軍殺將。

statement.id: Teks sejarah Shiji ini menyebut 天狗 sebagai tanda langit berbentuk seperti bintang jatuh besar, bersuara, yang bagian bawahnya jatuh ke bumi menyerupai anjing; tempat jatuhnya tampak seperti api yang menjulang, dan ia mengisyaratkan pasukan hancur serta jenderal terbunuh sejauh seribu li.
statement.en: This historical text, the Shiji, describes the 天狗 as a heavenly sign shaped like a great shooting star, with sound, whose lower part settles on the ground resembling a dog; where it falls it looks like blazing fire reaching heaven, and it portends armies broken and generals killed for a thousand li.

claims.quote: Zhang Xian (Chinese: 張仙; pinyin: Zhāng Xiān) is the enemy of the tiangou. ... He is the god of birth and the protector of male children. Many sought for him to give them male offspring and to protect their living sons.

statement.id: Zhang Xian adalah dewa kelahiran dan pelindung anak laki-laki; banyak orang memintanya memberi keturunan laki-laki dan melindungi putra-putra mereka yang hidup.
statement.en: Zhang Xian is the god of birth and the protector of male children; many sought him to give them male offspring and to protect their living sons.

claims.quote: Seeing this, a black dog that Hou Yi was rearing went inside her room and licked the remains of the pill. He then chased after Chang'e, getting bigger and bigger. Chang'e, terrified, hid on the Moon. The black dog then ate the Moon, along with Chang'e.

statement.id: Dalam legenda, seekor anjing hitam milik Hou Yi menjilat sisa pil keabadian di kamar Chang'e, mengejarnya sambil terus membesar, lalu memakan Bulan bersama Chang'e.
statement.en: In the legend, a black dog Hou Yi was rearing went into Chang'e's room and licked the remains of the immortality pill, chased after her getting bigger and bigger, and ate the Moon along with Chang'e.

claims.quote: Tiangou spat the Moon and Chang'e back out, and Chang'e continued living on the Moon.

statement.id: Menurut kisah itu, Tiangou memuntahkan kembali Bulan dan Chang'e, dan Chang'e terus hidup di Bulan.
statement.en: In the tale, Tiangou spat the Moon and Chang'e back out, and Chang'e continued living on the Moon.

short_description.id: Tianlong adalah naga terbang dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang juga nama bintang dan nama diri; dalam tradisi Mahayana ia menjaga Istana Langit.
short_description.en: Tianlong is a flying dragon in Chinese mythology, also a star and a proper name; in the Mahayana tradition it guards the Heavenly Palace.

long_description.id: Tianlong adalah naga terbang dalam mitologi Tiongkok, dan namanya juga dipakai untuk bintang dalam astrologi Tiongkok serta sebagai nama diri. Istilah ini menggabungkan unsur untuk langit dan naga. Tianlong juga sama bunyinya dengan Tianlong yang berarti Si Tuli Langit, pendamping Wenchang Wang.
long_description.en: Tianlong is a flying dragon in Chinese mythology, and the name is also used for a star in Chinese astrology and as a proper name. The term combines elements for heaven and dragon. Tianlong is also homophonous with Heavenly Deaf, an attendant of Wenchang Wang.

long_description.id: Dari arti awal naga langit, tianlong berkembang menjadi makna nāga langit atau dewa dan nāga. Kata ini baru tercatat pada zaman Han, meski langit dan naga dipakai bersama sejak tulisan zaman Zhou. Dalam tradisi Mahayana, tianlong adalah kelas nāga pertama dari empat kelas, yang menjaga Istana Langit dan memikulnya agar tidak jatuh.
long_description.en: From the original sense of heavenly dragon, tianlong developed the meanings of heavenly nāgas or devas and nāgas. The word is recorded only from the Han period, though heaven and dragon were used together in Zhou-period writings. In the Mahayana tradition, tianlong ranks first among four nāga classes; they watch over the Heavenly Palace and bear it up so that it never falls.

long_description.id: Teks Fanyi Mingyi Ji mengutip sebuah komentar yang membagi naga menjadi empat jenis, dengan jenis pertama menjaga istana langit dan patung naga dibuat di atas atap rumah manusia. Kamus Fangyan menyebut naga yang belum naik ke langit sebagai panlong. Tianlong juga nama bintang ketiga di Fangxiu yang setara dengan rasi Scorpius, dan ketika bintang naga muncul di langit lazim diadakan persembahan untuk memohon hujan.
long_description.en: The Fanyi Mingyi Ji text quotes a commentary dividing dragons into four kinds, the first guarding heavenly palaces, with dragon images made on human roofs. The Fangyan dictionary calls a dragon that has not yet ascended to heaven a panlong. Tianlong is also the name of the 3rd star in Fangxiu, matching the constellation Scorpius, and a sacrifice asking for rain was customarily made once the dragon star showed in the sky.

claims.quote: Tianlong (simplified Chinese: 天龙; traditional Chinese: 天龍; pinyin: tiānlóng; Wade–Giles: t'ien lung; lit. "heavenly dragon") is a flying dragon in Chinese mythology, a star in Chinese astrology, and a proper name.

statement.id: Tianlong adalah naga terbang dalam mitologi Tiongkok; nama yang sama juga memiliki penggunaan astronomis.
statement.en: Tianlong is a flying dragon in Chinese mythology, with the same name also used astronomically.

claims.quote: The term tianlong combines tian 天 "heaven" and long 龍 "dragon". Since tian literally means "heaven; the heavens; sky" or figuratively "Heaven; God; gods", tianlong can denote "heavenly dragon; celestial dragon" or "holy dragon; divine dragon".

statement.id: Namanya menggabungkan unsur langit dan naga.
statement.en: Its name combines elements for heaven and dragon.

claims.quote: Tianlong 天龍 is homophonous with another name in Chinese folklore. Tianlong 天聾 "Heavenly Deaf" (with the character long 聾 "deaf" combining the "ear radical" 耳 and a long 龍 phonetic element) and Diya 地啞 "Earthly Dumb" are legendary attendants to Wenchang Wang 文昌王, the patron deity of literature.

statement.id: Tianlong sang naga dibedakan dari Tianlong bermakna tuli surgawi, pengiring Wenchang Wang.
statement.en: The dragon Tianlong differs from the homonymous Heavenly Deaf attendant of Wenchang Wang.

claims.quote: From originally denoting "heavenly dragon", Tianlong 天龍 semantically developed meanings as Buddhist "heavenly Nāgas" or "Devas and Nāgas", "centipede", and "proper names" of stars, people, and places.

statement.id: Maknanya berkembang dalam Buddhisme menjadi naga surgawi atau kelompok dewa dan naga.
statement.en: Its Buddhist senses developed to include heavenly nagas or devas and nagas.

claims.quote: Among Chinese classic texts, tian "heaven" and long "dragon" were first used together in Zhou dynasty (1122 BCE – 256 BCE) writings, but the word tianlong was not recorded until the Han dynasty (207 BCE – 220 CE).

statement.id: Kata tianlong tercatat sejak zaman Han.
statement.en: The word tianlong is recorded from the Han period.

claims.quote: First, tianlong 天龍 means "heavenly dragon/nāga" as the first of four nāga classes in Mahayana tradition. ... who guard the Heavenly Palace and carry it so that it does not fall.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, dalam tradisi Mahayana tianlong adalah kelas nāga pertama dari empat kelas, yang menjaga Istana Langit dan memikulnya agar tidak jatuh.
statement.en: According to the article, in the Mahayana tradition tianlong is the first of four nāga classes, who guard the Heavenly Palace and carry it so that it does not fall.

claims.quote: Wolfram Eberhard notes, "When the dragon star appeared in the sky it was customary to make a sacrifice supplicating for rain," and this springtime dragon festival occurs on the 2nd day of the 2nd month.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, Eberhard mencatat bahwa ketika bintang naga muncul di langit, lazim diadakan persembahan untuk memohon hujan, dan festival naga musim semi itu jatuh pada hari kedua bulan kedua.
statement.en: According to the article, Eberhard notes that when the dragon star appeared in the sky it was customary to make a sacrifice supplicating for rain, and this springtime dragon festival occurs on the 2nd day of the 2nd month.

claims.quote: Tianlong 天龍 "Heavenly Dragon" is the 3rd star in Fangxiu 房宿 "Room (Chinese constellation)" and corresponds to the Western constellation Scorpius.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, Tianlong (天龍, Naga Langit) adalah bintang ketiga di Fangxiu (rumah Kamar) dan sepadan dengan rasi Barat Scorpius.
statement.en: According to the article, Tianlong (天龍, Heavenly Dragon) is the 3rd star in Fangxiu (the Room mansion) and corresponds to the Western constellation Scorpius.

statement.id: Teks Fanyi Mingyi Ji mengutip sebuah komentar yang menyebut naga ada empat jenis, yang pertama menjaga istana langit dan menahannya agar tidak jatuh; patung naga dibuat di atas atap rumah manusia, dan jenis lain membawa awan dan hujan, membuka sungai dan saluran, atau menjaga harta karun.
statement.en: The Fanyi Mingyi Ji text quotes a commentary saying dragons are of four kinds, the first guarding heavenly palaces and holding them so they do not fall; dragon images are made on human roofs, and the other kinds bring clouds and rain, open rivers and channels, or guard treasure.

claims.quote: 度高為揣。 半步為跬。 半盲為睺。 未陞天龍謂之蟠龍。 裔，夷狄之揔名。

statement.id: Kamus Fangyan menyatakan bahwa naga yang belum naik ke langit (未陞天龍) disebut panlong (蟠龍, naga melingkar).
statement.en: The Fangyan dictionary says a dragon that has not yet ascended to heaven (未陞天龍) is called a panlong (蟠龍, coiled dragon).

short_description.id: Tuchulcha adalah daemon dunia bawah dalam mitologi Etruria, bertelinga runcing, berambut ular, dan berparuh, yang hanya dikenal dari satu lukisan dinding makam di Tarquinia.
short_description.en: Tuchulcha is a chthonic daemon of Etruscan mythology with pointed ears, snake hair and a beak, known only from a single tomb wall painting at Tarquinia.

long_description.id: Tuchulcha adalah daemon dunia bawah dalam mitologi Etruria, bertelinga runcing (mungkin telinga keledai), berambut ular, dan berparuh (mungkin paruh burung nasar). Ia tinggal di dunia bawah bernama Aita. Satu-satunya gambaran yang diketahui adalah lukisan dinding di Makam Orcus II di Tarquinia.
long_description.en: Tuchulcha was a chthonic Etruscan daemon with pointed ears (perhaps a donkey's), hair of snakes and a beak (perhaps a vulture's). It lived in the underworld known as Aita. The only depiction known to us is a wall painting from the Tomb of Orcus II at Tarquinia.

long_description.id: Dalam lukisan makam itu, sosok ini muncul dalam episode kisah These (Theseus) yang mengunjungi dunia bawah, tempat ia dan sahabatnya Peirithous bermain papan permainan, dilayani oleh Tuchulcha. Sosok itu berbusana chiton sederhana dan memiliki paruh burung besar, telinga serigala atau keledai, dan ular menggeliat sebagai rambut.
long_description.en: In the tomb painting, the figure appears in an episode of the story of These (Theseus) visiting the underworld, where he and his friend Peirithous play a board game, attended by Tuchulcha. The figure wears a plain chiton and has a large bird's beak, wolf-like or donkey ears and snakes writhing as hair.

long_description.id: Para sarjana berselisih tentang jenis kelaminnya. Banyak yang menyebutnya laki-laki karena ciri maskulin seperti rambut wajah yang mirip janggut, sedangkan Nancy de Grummond menilainya sangat mungkin perempuan (atau tak berjenis kelamin) dan sebuah abstrak konferensi menilainya sengaja ambigu. Penanda belah ketupat pada ularnya dikenali sebagai ciri ular adder berbisa.
long_description.en: Scholars disagree about its sex. Many call it male because of masculine features such as facial hair resembling a beard, while Nancy de Grummond judges it very likely female (or neither gender) and a conference abstract judges it intentionally ambiguous. The diamond marking on its snakes has been identified as that of the poisonous adder.

long_description.id: Abstrak konferensi yang sama menyebut bahwa demon Etruria digambarkan sebagai makhluk chthonic ketika dipadukan dengan kisah mitologi Yunani pada lukisan makam, patung pemakaman, dan guci abu, serta berperan sebagai psychopomp pada lukisan makam dan sarkofagus.
long_description.en: The same conference abstract notes that Etruscan demons appear as underworld beings when woven into Greek myth scenes in tomb paintings, tomb statuary and cinerary urns, and that they also acted as guides of the dead (psychopomps) on paintings and sarcophagi.

short_description.id: Ubagabi adalah cahaya hantu dalam legenda Kawachi dan Tanba berupa bola api yang muncul pada malam hujan. Dikatakan ia berasal dari arwah nenek yang mencuri minyak.
short_description.en: The ubagabi is a ghost light in the legends of Kawachi and Tanba, a ball of fire appearing on rainy nights. It is said to originate from an old woman who stole oil.

long_description.id: Ubagabi (姥ヶ火 atau 姥火, "api nenek") adalah cahaya hantu atmosferik dalam legenda Provinsi Kawachi (kini Osaka) dan Tanba (kini Kyoto utara). Menurut Shokoku Rijin Dan, pada malam hujan di Hiraoka, Kawachi, ia muncul sebagai bola api sepanjang satu shaku. Yokai.com menggambarkannya bola api dengan wajah nenek di dalamnya.
long_description.en: The ubagabi (姥ヶ火 or 姥火, "old woman's fire") is an eerie ghost light of Kawachi Province (today's Osaka Prefecture) and Tanba Province (today's northern Kyoto Prefecture). The Shokoku Rijin Dan says that on a rainy night at Hiraoka in Kawachi it shows up as a fireball one shaku long. Yokai.com pictures a ball of flame with an old woman's face inside.

long_description.id: Dikatakan seorang nenek mencuri minyak dari Kuil Hiraoka dan menjadi api misterius oleh kutukan; Yokai.com menyebut ubagabi tercipta dari hantu nenek yang tertangkap mencuri minyak dan mati karena malu, dan kolam di belakang kuil disebut Ubagabi-ike. Dalam kisah lain nenek yang tenggelam dalam banjir menjadi api di dekat Sungai Hozu.
long_description.en: One tale says an old woman took oil from Hiraoka Shrine and, cursed for it, turned into a mysterious fire; Yokai.com says ubagabi are created from the ghosts of old women caught stealing oil who died of shame, and the pond behind the shrine is called Ubagabi-ike. In another tale an old woman who drowned in a flood became a flame near the Hozu River.

long_description.id: Seorang pejalan malam di Kawachi pernah dihantam wajahnya oleh ubagabi yang mendadak muncul, yang ternyata berupa burung mirip ayam; ketika terbang pergi ia kembali menjadi bola api, dan Mizuki Shigeru menduga ia sebenarnya burung. Menurut Yokai.com ia dapat terbang hingga 4 kilometer dalam sekejap, orang yang bahunya diserempet mati dalam tiga tahun, dan ia lenyap bila orang berseru "Abura-sashi!"
long_description.en: A night traveler in Kawachi once had his face struck by an ubagabi that appeared from nowhere and proved to be a chicken-like bird; when it flew away it turned back into a ball of fire, and Mizuki Shigeru suggested it might actually be a bird. According to Yokai.com it can fly up to 4 kilometers in an instant, a person whose shoulder it grazes dies within three years, and it vanishes if one shouts "Abura-sashi!"

short_description.id: Wani adalah monster laut atau naga dalam mitologi Jepang. Namanya ditulis dengan aksara "buaya", tetapi hakikatnya diperdebatkan: buaya, hiu, atau naga.
short_description.en: Wani is a sea monster or dragon in Japanese mythology. Its name is written with the character for "crocodile", but its nature is debated: crocodile, shark, or dragon.

long_description.id: Wani (鰐) adalah monster laut atau naga dalam mitologi Jepang. Karena ditulis dengan aksara 鰐, kata ini diterjemahkan "buaya", atau kadang "hiu". Teks klasik menulis namanya dengan aksara fonetik 和邇 dan aksara 鰐; Kojiki memakai wani sebagai nama diri dan sebagai monster laut dalam dua konteks.
long_description.en: Wani (鰐) is a sea monster or dragon in Japanese mythology. Because it is written with the character 鰐, the word is translated "crocodile", or sometimes "shark". Classical texts write its name with the phonetic characters 和邇 and the character 鰐; the Kojiki uses wani both as a proper name and as a sea monster in two contexts.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah kelinci putih dari Inaba, wani ditipu agar berbaris menyeberangi laut, dan wani yang terakhir melucuti kelinci itu. Dalam mitos Hoori dan Hoderi, dewa laut mengumpulkan semua wani dan memilih satu untuk mengantar putrinya yang hamil dan suaminya kembali ke daratan; sang putri kemudian berubah menjadi makhluk sepanjang delapan depa saat melahirkan. Nihongi juga memakai kata kuma-wani, termasuk untuk dewa laut Kotoshironushi sebagai "wani beruang" sepanjang delapan depa.
long_description.en: In the White Hare of Inaba tale, wani are tricked into lying in a row across the sea, and the last wani strips the hare. In the myth of Hoori and Hoderi, the sea god gathers all the wani and chooses one to escort his pregnant daughter and her husband back to land; the princess later turns into a creature eight fathoms long at childbirth. The Nihongi also uses the word kuma-wani, including for the sea god Kotoshiro-nushi as an eight-fathom "bear-wani".

long_description.id: Para penafsir berbeda pendapat. Chamberlain membela terjemahan "buaya" dan menilai wani makhluk amfibi mirip ular; Aston menilai wani hampir pasti naga Tiongkok yang hidup di laut; De Visser menyebutnya dewa laut Jepang kuno berwujud naga atau ular. Entri ensiklopedia Heibonsha menyebut wani dialek San'in untuk hiu besar dan memuat legenda wani menyusuri sungai dalam Izumo no Kuni Fudoki dan Hizen no Kuni Fudoki.
long_description.en: Interpreters disagree. Chamberlain defended the translation "crocodile" and judged the wani an amphibious serpent-like creature; Aston thought the wani almost certainly the Chinese dragon and a creature of the sea; De Visser called it an old Japanese dragon- or serpent-shaped sea-god. The Heibonsha encyclopedia entry calls wani a San'in dialect word for the large shark and records legends of a wani going up a river in the Izumo no Kuni Fudoki and the Hizen no Kuni Fudoki.

cultural_context.id: Wani muncul dalam mitos laut Jepang sebagai pengantar, penghuni istana dewa laut, dan wujud sejati sang putri dewa laut; sebuah entri ensiklopedia menyebut ikan itu mungkin dipandang suci.
cultural_context.en: Wani appear in Japanese sea myths as escorts, inhabitants of the sea god's realm, and the true form of the sea god's daughter; an encyclopedia entry suggests the fish was perhaps regarded as sacred.

literal_meaning.id: Ditulis dengan aksara 鰐 yang berarti "buaya; aligator"; karena itu wani diterjemahkan "buaya", atau kadang "hiu".
literal_meaning.en: Written with the kanji 鰐, from Chinese, meaning "crocodile; alligator"; hence wani is translated "crocodile", or sometimes "shark".

statement.en: The sea god's daughter makes a request concerning her shapeshifting into a wani, and at the moment of delivery she turns into a "crocodile" eight fathoms long that crawls and writhes about.

statement.en: The Nihongi uses the word kuma-wani ("bear-wani", i.e. giant or strong) and describes the sea god Kotoshiro-nushi as a ya-hiro no kuma-wani, an "8-fathom bear-wani".

short_description.id: Feitouman adalah sosok gaib Tiongkok yang kepalanya lepas dan terbang pada malam hari.
short_description.en: Feitouman is a Chinese supernatural figure whose head detaches and flies at night.

long_description.id: Feitouman adalah sosok gaib Tiongkok yang kepalanya lepas dan terbang pada malam hari. Sancai Tuhui menggambarkan manusia penerbang kepala di Jawa dengan mata tanpa pupil.
long_description.en: Feitouman is a Chinese supernatural figure whose head detaches and flies at night. Sancai Tuhui describes head-flying people in Java with eyes lacking pupils.

long_description.id: Kisah selatan memberi mereka tanda merah di leher, telinga mirip sayap, dan kepulangan pada fajar. Kisah menyebut penutupan tubuh dapat menghalangi kembalinya kepala dan menyebabkan kematian.
long_description.en: A southern account gives them red neck marks, winglike ears and a dawn return. Stories say covering the body can obstruct the head’s return and cause death.

long_description.id: Youyang Zazu mencatat orang-orang di lembah Lingnan yang kepalanya terbang, disebut feitou liaozi. Sehari sebelumnya lehernya berbekas seperti benang merah; malamnya kepala itu bersayap, lepas dari tubuh, dan mencari kepiting serta cacing di lumpur tepi sungai, lalu kembali menjelang fajar. Teks yang sama mengutip catatan tentang luomin di selatan dan bangsa yang dapat melepaskan kepala dan tangannya ke berbagai laut.
long_description.en: The Youyang Zazu records people in the valleys of Lingnan whose heads fly, called feitou liaozi. A day before, a red-thread-like mark appears on the neck; at night the head sprouts wings, leaves the body and hunts crabs and worms in the riverbank mud, returning near dawn. The same text cites accounts of the luomin of the south and of a people who could send their head and hands to different seas.

claims.quote: 飛頭蛮（ひとうばん）は、中国の妖怪。古典の記述によれば、通常は人間の姿と変わりないが、夜になると首（頭部）だけが胴体から離れて空中を飛び回るものとされる。

statement.id: Feitouman adalah sosok gaib Tiongkok yang kepalanya lepas dan terbang pada malam hari.
statement.en: Feitouman is a Chinese supernatural figure whose head detaches and flies at night.

claims.quote: 類書『三才図会』によれば、大闍婆国（だいしゃばこく、ジャワ島のこと）に、頭を飛ばす者がいる。目に瞳が無いのが特徴で、現地では虫落（むしおとし）、落民（らくみん、首が落ちる人の意）と呼ばれる。

statement.id: Sancai Tuhui menggambarkan manusia penerbang kepala di Jawa dengan mata tanpa pupil.
statement.en: Sancai Tuhui describes head-flying people in Java with eyes lacking pupils.

claims.quote: 唐代の書『南方異物誌』によれば、嶺南（中国南部からベトナムにかけての地方）の洞穴の中にいる飛頭蛮は、首に赤い傷跡があることが特徴で、夜には耳を翼のように使って飛び回り、虫を食べ、夜が明けると元の体に戻ってくるという。

statement.id: Kisah selatan memberi mereka tanda merah di leher, telinga mirip sayap, dan kepulangan pada fajar.
statement.en: A southern account gives them red neck marks, winglike ears and a dawn return.

claims.quote: 頭部の離れた体を見ると、体が冷たくなっていた上に呼吸も微かになっていたので、布団をかけたところ、やがて戻ってきた首が布団に遮られて胴に戻ることができず、呼吸を荒らげて苦しみだし、布団を取り去ると首が胴に戻って落ち着いたという。また、銅の盆で胴体を覆った人もいたが、その際には首が胴に戻れず、とうとう死んでしまったという。

statement.id: Kisah menyebut penutupan tubuh dapat menghalangi kembalinya kepala dan menyebabkan kematian.
statement.en: Stories say covering the body can obstruct the head’s return and cause death.

claims.quote: 嶺南溪洞中往往有飛頭者，故有飛頭獠子之號。頭將飛一日前，頸有痕匝，項如紅縷，妻子遂看守之。
claims.locator: 酉陽雜俎 卷四 境異

statement.id: Youyang Zazu (酉陽雜俎) mencatat bahwa di lembah-lembah Lingnan (嶺南) sering ada orang yang kepalanya terbang, sehingga muncul sebutan feitou liaozi (飛頭獠子); sehari sebelum kepalanya terbang, lehernya berbekas melingkar seperti benang merah, dan istri serta anaknya lalu menjaganya.
statement.en: The Youyang Zazu (酉陽雜俎) records that in the valleys of Lingnan (嶺南) there are often people whose heads fly, hence the name feitou liaozi (飛頭獠子); a day before the head flies, a ring-like mark like a red thread appears on the neck, and the wife and children then keep watch.

claims.quote: 其人及夜狀如病，頭忽生翼，脫身而去，乃於岸泥尋蟹蚓之類食，將曉飛還，如夢覺，其腹實矣。
claims.locator: 酉陽雜俎 卷四 境異

statement.id: Pada malam hari orang itu tampak seperti sakit, kepalanya tiba-tiba bersayap dan lepas dari tubuh, mencari kepiting dan cacing di lumpur tepi sungai untuk dimakan, lalu terbang kembali menjelang fajar; ia bangun seperti dari mimpi dengan perut kenyang.
statement.en: At night the person looks ill, the head suddenly sprouts wings and leaves the body to look for crabs and worms in the riverbank mud, then flies back near dawn; the person wakes as if from a dream with a full stomach.

claims.quote: 《於氏誌怪》：南方落民，其頭能飛。其俗所祠，名曰蟲落，因號落民。
claims.locator: 酉陽雜俎 卷四 境異

statement.id: Mengutip Yu shi zhiguai (於氏誌怪), teks itu menyebut "luomin" (落民) di selatan yang kepalanya dapat terbang; pemujaan mereka bernama chongluo (蟲落), sehingga mereka disebut luomin.
statement.en: Quoting the Yu shi zhiguai (於氏誌怪), the text mentions the "luomin" (落民) of the south whose heads can fly; their worship is called chongluo (蟲落), hence the name luomin.

claims.quote: 《王子年拾遺》言：漢武時，因墀國使南方，有解形之民，能先使頭飛南海，左手飛東海，右手飛西澤。
claims.locator: 酉陽雜俎 卷四 境異

statement.id: Mengutip Shiyi ji (拾遺) karya Wang Zinian, pada masa Han Wudi ada bangsa yang dapat melepaskan bagian tubuhnya: kepala terbang ke Laut Selatan, tangan kiri ke Laut Timur, dan tangan kanan ke rawa barat.
statement.en: Quoting Wang Zinian’s Shiyi ji (拾遺), in the time of Emperor Wu of Han there was a people who could detach their bodies: the head flew to the Southern Sea, the left hand to the Eastern Sea and the right hand to the western marsh.
